nahhas-irab:12-12.t: وَلَكُمْ نِصْفُ ما تَرَكَ أَزْواجُكُمْ: [nominative] by ibtidāʾ (being the mubtadaʾ, subject) or by the ṣifa [Translator's note: i.e. by the prepositional phrase لكم, in the Kufan terminology]. Saʿīd al-Akhfash said concerning وَإِنْ كانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلالَةً: if you wish, you make كلالة accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كان; and if you wish, you make كان mean "occurred" and make يورث an adjective (ṣifa) of رجل, with كلالة accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), as you say: يُضرَب قائما ("he is beaten while standing"). Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Akhfash spoke on the basis that al-kalāla is the deceased; if it refers to the heirs, you would supply it as "possessing kalāla" (ذا كلالة). أَوِ امْرَأَةٌ: one also says مرأة, and that is the original form. وَلَهُ أَخٌ: the original is أخو, as shown by أخوان; something was dropped from it and it was altered irregularly. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: something was dropped from it for firmness [Translator's note: «للتثبّت» as in the source], and the original of أخت is أخوة. Al-Farrāʾ said: the first letter of أخت takes a ḍamma because what was dropped from it is a wāw, and the first letter of بنت takes a kasra because what was dropped from it is a yāʾ. فَلِكُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ: [nominative] by ibtidāʾ or by the ṣifa. غَيْرَ مُضَارٍّ: accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. he makes a bequest with it while not causing harm (غير مضارّ); and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made clear that one who bequeaths more than a third is causing harm. وَصِيَّةٍ: a maṣdar (verbal noun). وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ: i.e. of whoever obeys Him. حَلِيمٌ: i.e. towards whoever disobeys Him. As for His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً, it was said that its meaning is: «عليما» of what benefit there is for you in it, «حكيما» in how He has apportioned these properties. Al-Ḥasan said: «إنّ الله كان عليما» of His creation before He created them, «حكيما» in how He governs them.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ: a condition (sharṭ). يُدْخِلْهُ: the requital (mujāzāh, i.e. the apodosis). In ordinary speech يدخلهم would also be allowed, according to the sense, and من يطيعون would also be allowed.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
وَاللَّاتِي يَأْتِينَ الْفاحِشَةَ مِنْ نِسائِكُمْ: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is فَاسْتَشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ أَرْبَعَةً مِنْكُمْ.
اللاتي can only refer to women. فَإِنْ شَهِدُوا فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ فِي الْبُيُوتِ. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have explained that this is abrogated. When a woman committed fornication she used to be confined, and that was abrogated by the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ: «قد جعل الله لهنّ سبيلا» ("Allah has made a way for them"). Were it not for the ḥadīth, confinement would have been obligatory along with flogging. Confinement was abrogated for the married (muḥṣana) adulteress by stoning, and stoning is Sunna; so the ḥadīth has abrogated the Qur'an, indisputably.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
وَالَّذانِ يَأْتِيانِها مِنْكُمْ: the more appropriate view is that this refers to two men. As for its referring to a man and a woman, with the masculine given precedence over the feminine, that is far-fetched, because one does not take a thing out into figurative usage when its meaning is sound in its literal sense. Some claimed that His saying فَآذُوهُما is abrogated; and it was said — and this is more appropriate:
it is not abrogated, and it is obligatory that they be hurt by reproach, so it is said to them: "You have committed immorality, you have transgressed, and you have contravened the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He."

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: إِنَّمَا التَّوْبَةُ عَلَى اللَّهِ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السُّوءَ بِجَهالَةٍ: it was said: this is for everyone who commits a sin; and it was said: this is only for whoever was ignorant, while repentance for everyone who commits a sin is in another place.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
Abū Jaʿfar said: the verse is difficult, and the iʿrāb makes its meaning clear. His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, وَلَا الَّذِينَ يَمُوتُونَ وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الذين يعملون السيئات. There are three views on its meaning:
Most people hold that the meaning of السيئات here is what is short of disbelief, i.e. repentance is not for one who committed evil deeds short of disbelief and then repented at the time of death, nor for one who died a disbeliever and then repents on the Day of Resurrection. It is also possible that the meaning of «ولا الذين يموتون» is: nor those who are close to death. And it was said: those who commit evil deeds are the disbelievers and others, and then the disbelievers are singled out, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: فِيهِما فاكِهَةٌ وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ [al-Raḥmān: 68]. A third view: those who commit evil deeds are the disbelievers, so the meaning is: repentance is not for the disbelievers who repent at the time of death, nor for those who die while they are disbelievers.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَرِثُوا النِّساءَ كَرْهاً: أَنْ is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "inheriting women" (وراثة النساء). والنِّساءَ: [Translator's note: the source reads «منصوبات على أحد معنيين يكون بمعنى أن ترثوا من النساء كما ترثون الأموال»; only one of the two meanings is stated, and the text appears defective here] accusative according to one of two meanings: it may mean that you inherit from women, [or] as you inherit property; both have been transmitted in tafsīr. Abū Ṣāliḥ related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: when Abū Qays ibn al-Aslat died, his son came and threw his cloak over his father's wife and said: "I have inherited her as I inherited his property." This was their custom: if he wished, he consummated marriage with her without a dowry, and if he wished, he married her off and took her dowry. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَرِثُوا النِّساءَ كَرْهاً.
In another narration: a man would marry a woman, and if he died leaving her before consummating the marriage, his son would prevent her from marrying until he inherited from her. كَرْهاً: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَلا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ: it may be conjoined (maʿṭūf) — and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is ولا أن تعضلوهنّ — and it may be that «كرها» completes the statement, and then He began the prohibition afresh, saying «ولا تعضلوهنّ». That is when a man has a wife whom he does not want, so he obstructs her (yaʿḍuluhā), i.e. he does not divorce her so that she ransoms herself from him; that is forbidden to him. Ibn al-Salmānī said: لا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَرِثُوا النِّساءَ كَرْهاً was revealed concerning the practice of the Jāhiliyya, and وَلا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ was revealed concerning the practice of Islam. Ibn Sīrīn and Abū Qilāba said: it is not lawful for him to take a ransom from her unless he finds a man upon her belly; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda said:
the manifest indecency is nushūz (recalcitrance), i.e. if she is recalcitrant he may take the ransom. A third view: إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ means unless they commit fornication, in which case they are confined in the houses, so this was before the abrogation. «وأن» is in the position of the accusative on all the views, because it is an exception not from the first [category] (istithnāʾ laysa min al-awwal, i.e. a disjoined exception).

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: أَتَأْخُذُونَهُ بُهْتاناً: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَإِثْماً: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. مُبِيناً: its adjective (naʿt).

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: وَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَهُ وَقَدْ أَفْضى بَعْضُكُمْ إِلى بَعْضٍ: a clause in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
وَلا تَنْكِحُوا ما نَكَحَ آباؤُكُمْ مِنَ النِّساءِ إِلَّا ما قَدْ سَلَفَ: an exception not from the first [category] (i.e. a disjoined exception).
إِنَّهُ كانَ فاحِشَةً: the khabar (predicate) of كان; the nominative would be allowed, by treating «كان» as inoperative, outside the Qur'an. وَساءَ سَبِيلًا: accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz, specification).

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهاتُكُمْ: the plural of أمّهة; one says أمّ and أمّهة with the same meaning, and the Qur'an has come with both. أُمَّهاتُكُمْ: the noun of a verb whose agent is not named, standing in place of the fāʿil (i.e. nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: because together with the verb it forms a clause just as the agent does, and the verb cannot do without it just as it cannot do without the agent. وَبَناتُكُمْ: conjoined; plural of بنة, whose original form is بنية, while the forms in use are ابنة and بنت. Al-Farrāʾ said: the bāʾ of بنت takes a kasra so that the kasra indicates the omission of the yāʾ. وَأَخَواتُكُمْ: conjoined; plural of أخوة. وَعَمَّاتُكُمْ: conjoined to it, up to His saying وَأَنْ تَجْمَعُوا بَيْنَ الْأُخْتَيْنِ: «أن» is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "and combining two sisters has been forbidden to you". إِلَّا ما قَدْ سَلَفَ: an exception not from the first [category] (i.e. a disjoined exception).

nahhas-irab:159-159.t: وَإِنْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ إِلَّا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ: because the People of the Book are of two kinds regarding him: some of them called him a liar and some of them took him as a god, so each is compelled before his death to believe in him, because it becomes clear to him that he was upon falsehood when he sees [the truth] with his own eyes. Sībawayh's implied form (taqdīr) is: "And there is not one (أحد) of the People of the Book but he will surely believe in him"; the Kufans' implied form is: "And there is none of the People of the Book except one who (من) will surely believe in him" — and omitting the relative noun is an error. وَيَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيداً: that is, over those who were among them.

nahhas-irab:160-160.t: فَبِظُلْمٍ مِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: this is a badal (substitute) for فَبِما نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثاقَهُمْ [verse 155]. حَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِمْ طَيِّباتٍ أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ: such as every animal with claws/undivided hoofs and what resembles it. وَبِصَدِّهِمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ كَثِيراً: that is, a great deal of hindering (صدّا كثيرا).

nahhas-irab:162-162.t:
لكِنِ الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ: nominative by being the mubtadaʾ (subject). يُؤْمِنُونَ is in the position of the khabar (predicate); the Kufans say: it is nominative by virtue of the pronoun. وَالْمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلاةَ: there are six views on its accusative. Sībawayh puts it in the accusative as praise (ʿalā al-madḥ), i.e. "and I mean the ones who establish (المقيمين)". Sībawayh said: "This is the chapter of what is put in the accusative as glorification (al-taʿẓīm), and among it is المقيمين الصلاة", and he recited: [al-Basīṭ metre] 111-
وكلّ قوم أطاعوا أمر مرشدهم ... إلّا نميرا أطاعت أمر غاويها
الظّاعنين ولمّا يظعنوا أحدا ... والقائلون لمن دار نخلّيها
(Every people obeyed the command of their right guide, except Numayr, who obeyed the command of their misleader — those who move off though they have yet to make anyone move off, and who say: "For whom is a dwelling that we abandon?")
And he recited: [al-Kāmil metre] 112-
لا يبعدن قومي الذين هم ... سمّ العداة وآفة الجزر
النّازلين بكلّ معترك ... والطّيبون معاقد الأزر
(May my people not perish, who are poison to the enemies and the bane of the slaughter-camels — those who dismount in every battlefield, and pure are they where the waist-wrappers are tied.)
This is the soundest of what has been said about المقيمين. Al-Kisāʾī said: وَالْمُقِيمِينَ is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «ما». Abū Jaʿfar said: this is far-fetched, because the meaning would then be "and they believe in the ones who establish [prayer]". Muḥammad ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī] reported that it has been said that المقيمين here are the angels, peace be upon them, because of their constancy in prayer, glorification and seeking forgiveness, and he chose this view; and he reported that the accusative as praise is far-fetched, because praise comes only after the khabar is complete, and the khabar of الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ is in أُولئِكَ سَنُؤْتِيهِمْ أَجْراً عَظِيماً, so it cannot be put in the accusative as praise while the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is not yet complete — because he made «والمؤتون» conjoined and made the khabar what was mentioned. Sībawayh's position is other than what he said. It has also been said: والمقيمين is conjoined to the kāf in قبلك, i.e. "before you and before the ones who establish"; and it has been said: «والمقيمين» is conjoined to the kāf in أولئك; and it has been said: it is conjoined to the hāʾ and mīm, i.e. "of them and of the ones who establish". These three answers are not permissible, because in them an overt noun is conjoined to a genitive pronoun. The sixth answer is that «المقيمين» is conjoined to قبلك, the meaning being "and before the ones who establish"; then المقيمين was put in the place of قبل, just as He said وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82]. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read it as والمقيمون الصلاة, and so it is in the reading (ḥarf) of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd; as for the reading of Ubayy, in it it is وَالْمُقِيمِينَ, as in the codices. وَالْمُؤْتُونَ: there are five views on it. Sībawayh said: as for «المؤتون», it is nominative by being the mubtadaʾ. Someone else said: it is nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "so they are the givers of zakat". It has been said: it is conjoined to the pronoun latent in المقيمين; and it has been said: it is conjoined to the pronoun in يؤمنون, i.e. "they believe, they and the givers". The fifth answer is that it is conjoined to الراسخين.

nahhas-irab:163-163.t: إِنَّا أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ كَما أَوْحَيْنا إِلى نُوحٍ: نوح is fully declined (munṣarif) though it is a foreign name, because it consists of three letters and so is light. As for إِبْراهِيمَ وَإِسْماعِيلَ وَإِسْحاقَ, they are foreign and definite, and therefore diptote; likewise يعقوب, عيسى and موسى — except that in عيسى and موسى the alif may be [the alif] of the feminine, in which case they are diptote whether definite or indefinite. It is reported from al-Ḥasan that he read ويونس with a kasra on the nūn, and likewise يوسف with a kasra on the sīn, deriving them from أنس and أسف; on this view they would have to be fully declined and pronounced with hamza, and their plurals would be يأ أنس and يأ اسف; whoever does not pronounce the hamza says يوانس and يواسف. Abū Zayd reported: يونس and يوسف.

nahhas-irab:164-164.t:
وَرُسُلًا قَدْ قَصَصْناهُمْ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ: [accusative] by an implied verb, i.e. "and We narrated messengers", because it is conjoined to something on which a verb has already acted. Similar to it is what Sībawayh recited: [al-Munsariḥ metre] 113-
أصبحت لا أحمل السّلاح ولا ... أملك رأس البعير إن نفرا
والذّئب أخشاه إن مررت به ... وحدي وأخشى الرّياح والمطرا
(I have become one who cannot carry weapons, nor control the camel's head if it bolts; and the wolf — I fear it if I pass by it alone, and I fear the winds and the rain.)
It is also possible that وَرُسُلًا is conjoined according to the meaning, because the meaning of إِنَّا أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ is "We sent you, revealing to you, and We sent messengers whom We have narrated to you before". In the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy it is ورسل, in the nominative. وَكَلَّمَ اللَّهُ مُوسى تَكْلِيماً: an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun). The grammarians agree that when you emphasise a verb with the maṣdar it is not figurative, and that in the poet's words: [al-Rajaz metre] 114-
امتلأ الحوض وقال قطني
(The cistern filled up and said: "Enough for me.")
it is not permissible to say "قال قولا" (it said a saying); likewise, since He said تكليما, it must be speech in the real sense, of the speech that is understood.

nahhas-irab:165-165.t: رُسُلًا مُبَشِّرِينَ: as a badal (substitute) for وَرُسُلًا قَدْ قَصَصْناهُمْ. It may also be by an implied verb, and it may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and messengers".

nahhas-irab:166-166.t: لكِنِ اللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ: nominative; and if you wish you may make the nūn doubled (لكنّ) and use the accusative. يَشْهَدُ بِما أَنْزَلَ إِلَيْكَ: the witness is the one who makes his testimony clear — that he makes clear and knows that. وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً.

nahhas-irab:167-168.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: the noun of «إنّ», and the clause is the khabar (predicate); likewise إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَظَلَمُوا. وَلا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ طَرِيقاً: a second object, from which «إلى» has been omitted, just as «من» was omitted in His words وَاخْتارَ مُوسى قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلًا [al-Aʿrāf: 155].

nahhas-irab:169-170.t:
إِلَّا طَرِيقَ جَهَنَّمَ: badal (substitute).
فَآمِنُوا خَيْراً لَكُمْ: on Sībawayh's position, "and bring about (وآتوا) what is better for you"; on al-Farrāʾ's view, it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a belief better for you"; and on Abū ʿUbayda's view: "it will be (يكن) better for you".

nahhas-irab:171-171.t:
يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ: a vocative with a muḍāf (genitive construct). لا تَغْلُوا فِي دِينِكُمْ: a prohibition; ghuluww is overstepping in wrongdoing. إِنَّمَا الْمَسِيحُ: nominative by being the mubtadaʾ (subject); عِيسَى is a badal (substitute) for it, and likewise ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ; it [ابن مريم] may also be the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, the meaning being: "the Messiah is only the son of Maryam, so how could he be a god, when he is originated, not eternal?", and رَسُولُ اللَّهِ would then be a second khabar. فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ: that is, that He is one God, the Creator of the Messiah and the One who sent him. وَلا تَقُولُوا ثَلاثَةٌ: that is, "and do not say: our gods are three". انْتَهُوا خَيْراً لَكُمْ: Sībawayh said:
"Among what is put in the accusative by implying the verb whose expression has been abandoned is His words انْتَهُوا خَيْراً لَكُمْ, because when you say 'desist' (انته) you are taking him out of one thing and putting him into another." And he recited: [al-Sarīʿ metre] 115-
فواعديه سرحتي مالك ... أو الرّبى بينهما أسهلا
(So make an appointment with him at Mālik's two lote-trees, or the hillocks between them — [coming to] what is easier.)
Abū ʿUbayda's position is: "desist, it will be (يكن) better for you". Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: this is an error, because one does not imply both the condition and its apodosis, and this is not found in the speech of the Arabs. Al-Farrāʾ's position is that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān [al-Akhfash the younger] said: this is a gross error, because the meaning would be "desist with the desisting that is better for you". إِنَّمَا اللَّهُ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ: mubtadaʾ and khabar. سُبْحانَهُ: a maṣdar (verbal noun). أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ: in the position of an accusative, i.e. "how could He have a child?" — a man's child resembles him, and there is nothing resembling Allah, Mighty and Majestic. وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا: explanation (bayān) [i.e. tamyīz (specification)], or, if you wish, a ḥāl (circumstantial); and the meaning of وكيل is "sufficient for His friends".

nahhas-irab:172-172.t:
ْ يَسْتَنْكِفَ الْمَسِيحُ
that is, he will not disdain. نْ يَكُونَ عَبْداً لِلَّهِ
in the position of an accusative, i.e. "from (من) being a servant of Allah". لَا الْمَلائِكَةُ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ
By this He indicated that the angels are superior to the prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them, and likewise وَلا أَقُولُ إِنِّي مَلَكٌ [Hūd: 31].
[Translator's note: the Quranic words at the start of each line are truncated in the source (لَنْ يَسْتَنْكِفَ، أَنْ يَكُونَ، وَلَا الْمَلائِكَةُ); they are reproduced as written.]

nahhas-irab:173-173.t: فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ: nominative by being the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is the khabar (predicate); it may also be accusative by an implied verb explained by what follows; likewise وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ اسْتَنْكَفُوا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا. We have already mentioned the meaning of calling ʿĪsā ﷺ "the Word". Among the best of what has been said about it is that since ʿĪsā ﷺ was a means of guidance, he became like the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by which guidance is obtained; and since through him [people] were brought to life from the death of disbelief, he was called the Spirit of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by way of likeness.

nahhas-irab:174-174.t: وَأَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكُمْ نُوراً مُبِيناً: that is, by which one is guided away from error; so it is a clear light (نور مبين), i.e. plain and evident.

nahhas-irab:175-175.t: فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَاعْتَصَمُوا بِهِ: that is, they protected themselves by His Book from disobeying Him; and when they hold fast to His Book they have held fast to Him. وَيَهْدِيهِمْ إِلَيْهِ: that is, to His reward.

nahhas-irab:176-176.t: يَسْتَفْتُونَكَ قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِي الْكَلالَةِ: there are three views on it: one is that al-kalāla is the deceased who has neither parent nor child; another is that it is the heirs among whom there is neither parent nor child; and it has been said: al-kalāla is the wealth. إِنِ امْرُؤٌ هَلَكَ: nominative by an implied verb; this is permitted because «إن» is the root of the conditional particles, and after it comes a past verb. يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا: in the position of an accusative — and it has been said: genitive — and there are three views on it. Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. "so that you do not (لئلا) go astray"; this is an error according to the Basrans, because «لا» is not omitted here. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] and a group of the Basrans said: the implied form is "out of aversion (كراهة) that you go astray", then [كراهة] was omitted, and it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The third view: the meaning is "Allah makes clear to you the going astray", i.e. when He has made clear to you what going astray is, you avoid it. وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ: mubtadaʾ and khabar, i.e. He is possessed of knowledge of everything concerning the welfare of His servants in the division of their inheritances and other matters.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
وَالْمُحْصَناتُ مِنَ النِّساءِ: conjoined (maʿṭūf); we have explained that they are women who have husbands. One says امرأة محصنة, i.e. married; and محصنة, i.e. free — and from this is وَالْمُحْصَناتُ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِناتِ وَالْمُحْصَناتُ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ [al-Māʾida: 5] — and محصنة, محصنة and حصان, i.e. chaste, as Ḥassān ibn Thābit said of ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: [al-Ṭawīl] 95-
حصان رزان ما تزنّ بريبة ... وتصبح غرثى من لحوم الغوافل
(Chaste, composed, never suspected of anything doubtful; she wakes up hungry for the flesh of heedless women — i.e. she never backbites them.)
The origin of this is their saying مدينة حصينة, i.e. impregnable. So the muḥṣana who has a husband is one whom her husband has prevented from marrying anyone else; the muḥṣana who is free is so because iḥṣān comes about through her; and the chaste woman is the one who holds herself back from immorality. إِلَّا ما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ: an exception from an affirmative statement. كِتابَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ: a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative, according to the view of Sībawayh; and it was said: it is an incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "hold fast to the Book of Allah". The nominative is allowed, i.e. "this is the ordinance of Allah". وَأُحِلَّ لَكُمْ ما وَراءَ ذلِكُمْ: i.e. Allah prescribed that for you and made lawful for you; and it is read وَأُحِلَّ لَكُمْ, referring back to حرّمت عليكم [Translator's note: the two readings are printed identically in the source; the second is evidently the passive reading «وأُحِلَّ» against an active «وأَحَلَّ»]. ما وَراءَ ذلِكُمْ: a mafʿūl (object). أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا: a badal (substitute) for «ما»; and the meaning may be "so that" (لأن), with the lām omitted, so that «أن» is in the position of the accusative or the genitive. مُحْصِنِينَ: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). فَمَا اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْهُنَّ: a condition (sharṭ), and the answer is فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ. فَرِيضَةً: a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:25-25.t:
وَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنْكُمْ طَوْلًا: a mafʿūl (object). أَنْ يَنْكِحَ: in the position of the accusative, i.e. "to [the point of] marrying" (إلى أن ينكح). وَالْمُحْصَناتِ: free women, not slave women; so of what your right hands possess — let him marry from this category.
بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). It may also be nominative by ينكح — "let some of you marry from others", i.e. let this one marry that one's maid — so it would be placed earlier and later [Translator's note: i.e. with a transposition of word order], i.e. "whoever among you cannot afford to marry the believing free women, let some of you marry from others, from your believing maids"; and «بعضكم» on this interpretation is nominative, construed according to the sense. فَإِذا أُحْصِنَّ: [this reading] is authentically reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, and he explained it as:
"they are married". Ibn Masʿūd said: فَإِذا أُحْصِنَّ, i.e. "they become Muslim". ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī said: فَإِذا أُحْصِنَّ, i.e. "they have protected themselves". This is the best of what has been said about this reading. Hārūn the Reader said: Maʿmar related to us, saying: I asked al-Zuhrī about His saying «فإذا أحصنّ» or «أحصنّ» [Translator's note: the two forms are not distinguished in the printed text; one is evidently «أُحْصِنَّ» and the other «أَحْصَنَّ»], and he said:
"The reading is «أحصنّ», and the meaning of أحصنّ is 'they are chaste'"; and it was said: "they become Muslim". Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not known from al-Zuhrī except by this chain, and it has no sound meaning: it cannot be "and when they are chaste, فَإِنْ أَتَيْنَ بِفاحِشَةٍ"; likewise it is far-fetched to say مِنْ فَتَياتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِناتِ "and when they become Muslim". The sound report is what he [Maʿmar] related from al-Zuhrī; he said: I asked him about the slave woman who commits fornication, and he said: "If she is married, she is flogged by the Book; if she is not married, she is flogged by the Sunna." Maʿmar related from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī, that the Prophet ﷺ was asked about the slave woman who is not muḥṣana, and he said: «إن زنت فاجلدوها ثم إن زنت فاجلدوها ثم إن زنت فاجلدوها، ثم قال في الثالثة أو الرابعة وبيعوها ولو بضفير» ("If she commits fornication, flog her; then if she commits fornication, flog her; then if she commits fornication, flog her" — then he said at the third or fourth time — "and sell her, even for a plaited rope"). This makes clear that when Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made obligatory upon the slave woman who commits fornication, having been married, half the punishment of the free woman, her case when she had not married was unclear to them, so they asked about it and were answered that she bears what the married one bears. So it is clear from this that iḥṣān here is marriage. It has also been said that the meaning is: "they bear half of what the muḥṣanāt bear of punishment", meaning by that married women; and that the married free woman, if she commits fornication, bears a hundred lashes by the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and stoning by the Sunna of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and stoning cannot be halved, so it follows that she bears half the flogging. وَأَنْ تَصْبِرُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ: mubtadaʾ and khabar, i.e. "patience is better for you". وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ: mubtadaʾ and khabar.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ: i.e. to make clear to you the matter of your religion, what is lawful for you and what is forbidden to you. After this He said يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُخَفِّفَ عَنْكُمْ [al-Nisāʾ: 28], so this came with أن and the first with the lām. Al-Farrāʾ said: the Arabs bring the lām in the sense of كي in the place of أن with أردت and أمرت; they say أردت أن تفعل and أردت لتفعل, because both seek the future. ظننت لتفعل is not allowed, because you say ظننت أن قد قمت. Abū Isḥāq said: this is a mistake; if the lām meant «أن», another lām would enter upon it, just as you say جئت كي تكرمني and then say جئت لتكرمني; and he recited to us: [al-Ṭawīl] 96-
أردت لكيما يعلم النّاس أنّها ... سراويل قيس والوفود شهود
(I wanted the people to know that they were Qays's trousers, while the delegations were witnesses.)
He said: the implied form is "He intended by it to make clear to you". Abū Jaʿfar said: the matter went further than this, until some of the Readers called it "the lām of «أن»". It was also said: the meaning is "Allah wants this for the sake of making clear to you", like وَأُمِرْتُ لِأَعْدِلَ بَيْنَكُمُ [al-Shūrā: 15]. وَيَهْدِيَكُمْ سُنَنَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ: one of the theorists said: in this there is evidence that everything forbidden to us before this verse had been forbidden to those before us. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a mistake, because the meaning may be "and He makes clear to you the affair of those before you who used to avoid what was forbidden", and it may be "He makes clear to you as He made clear to the prophets before you", without pointing to this specific thing.

nahhas-irab:27-28.t: وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and أن is in the position of the accusative governed by يريد; likewise يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُخَفِّفَ عَنْكُمْ. وَخُلِقَ الْإِنْسانُ: the noun of a verb whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). ضَعِيفاً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Its meaning is that his desire inclines him, and his lust and anger make him light-headed, and this is the most severe weakness, so he needed lightening.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْباطِلِ: i.e. by wrongdoing; gambling and everything prohibited enters into this. إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجارَةً عَنْ تَراضٍ مِنْكُمْ: this [with the nominative تجارةٌ] [Translator's note: the source prints the same vocalised form for both readings] is the reading of the people of Medina and of Abū ʿAmr; the Kufans read تِجارَةً in the accusative, and that is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. Abū Jaʿfar said: the accusative is far-fetched from the point of view of meaning and of iʿrāb. As for the meaning, this described trade does not involve consuming property wrongfully, so that the accusative would be [warranted]; and as for the iʿrāb, it requires the nominative, because «أن» here is in the position of the accusative, being an exception not from the first [category], and «تكون» is its ṣila; and the Arabs use it here in the sense of "occurred", saying جاءني القوم إلّا أن يكون زيد, and the accusative is hardly known. وَلا تَقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ: a prohibition. إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيماً: i.e. it is through His mercy that He forbade you this and restrained some of you from others.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ: i.e. whoever kills himself; and the meaning may be: whoever does anything of what was previously prohibited. فَسَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِ ناراً: the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness. وَكانَ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيراً: the noun of كان and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: إِنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبائِرَ: plural of كبيرة; the plural has a hamza because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the yāʾ had no share in taking a vowel, so it [the hamza] took the vowel. The meaning of اجتنبت الشيء is "I left the thing aside (jāniban)". نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئاتِكُمْ وَنُدْخِلْكُمْ: conjoined (maʿṭūf). Outside the Qur'an the accusative is allowed: by ṣarf (divergence) according to the Kufans, and by an implied «أن» according to the Basrans; and the nominative is allowed by cutting it off from the first. Abū ʿAmr and most of the Kufans read وَنُدْخِلْكُمْ مُدْخَلًا, which is the maṣdar (verbal noun); and the people of Medina and ʿĀṣim read وَنُدْخِلْكُمْ مُدْخَلًا, meaning "so you enter a noble place of entry". [Translator's note: the two readings are printed identically in the source; the reading of the people of Medina is «مَدْخَلًا», with fatḥa on the mīm.]

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: قُلْ أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لا [Translator's note: this quotation is from Āl ʿImrān 3:32 and appears in the source here in error; the discussion that follows concerns 4:32, وَلا تَتَمَنَّوْا ما فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بِهِ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ]. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, forbade envy. The Arabs say حسد فلان فلانا when someone wishes that the other's wealth would pass to him. The implied form is: "and do not wish for the transfer of that by which Allah has favoured some of you over others". If he wishes to have the like of his wealth without its passing away from him, it is said غبطه ("he admired him with emulation"), not حسده ("he envied him"). وَسْئَلُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ: al-Kisāʾī read وسلوا without hamza, casting the vowel of the hamza onto the sīn. إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيماً: i.e. He knows what is good for you, so let not some of you envy others.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: وَلِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنا مَوالِيَ: when «كلّ» comes on its own, there must be an omission in the speech according to all the grammarians, to the point that some of them allowed مررت بكلّ يا فتى ("I passed by all, O lad"), like «قبل» and «بعد». The implied omission is "and for each one (أحد) We have appointed heirs". Another answer is: "and for each thing of what parents and relatives leave We have appointed mawālī", i.e. heirs, i.e. those most entitled to the inheritance. والذين عاقدت أيمانكم: i.e. by oath. Ḥamza read وَالَّذِينَ عَقَدَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ, i.e. by oath. And Ḥamza read والّذين عقدت أيمانكم [Translator's note: the mention of Ḥamza's reading is repeated in the source], and it is a far-fetched reading, because mutual pledging (al-muʿāqada) only takes place between two or more, so its pattern is fāʿala. Ḥamza's reading is allowable on an obscure point of Arabic: its implied form would be "and those whom your right hands bound with the oath (عقدتهم أيمانكم الحلف)", the verb being transitive to two objects; and the implied form is "your right hands bound the oath for them (عقدت لهم أيمانكم الحلف)", then the lām was omitted, like وَإِذا كالُوهُمْ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 3], i.e. "they measured for them" (كالوا لهم); and the first object was omitted because it is attached [as a pronoun] within the ṣila (relative clause). فَآتُوهُمْ نَصِيبَهُمْ: there are two views on it. Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: it is abrogated by the laws of inheritance; and it was said: it is abrogated by His saying أُولُوا الْأَرْحامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلى بِبَعْضٍ فِي كِتابِ اللَّهِ [al-Anfāl: 75] — and these two are one view. The other view is that Mujāhid said: its meaning is "give them their share of support as you promised them", i.e. it is not abrogated. Abū Jaʿfar said: Mujāhid's view is more appropriate, because when the recitation is established, abrogation does not occur except by consensus or proof. إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيداً: i.e. He has witnessed your pledging with them, and He, Mighty and Majestic is He, loves the fulfilment [of pledges].

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
الرِّجالُ قَوَّامُونَ عَلَى النِّساءِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. they undertake maintaining them and defending them. One says قوّام and قيّم. بِما فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ: «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and that is why it needs no resumptive pronoun. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has favoured men over women with soundness of intellect and good management. وَبِما أَنْفَقُوا مِنْ أَمْوالِهِمْ: in dowries, until they became wives to them and their maintenance became an obligation on them. فَالصَّالِحاتُ قانِتاتٌ: mubtadaʾ [and] khabar. Al-Farrāʾ said: in the text (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh it is فالصالحات قوانت حوافظ. Abū Jaʿfar said:
this is a broken plural reserved for the feminine. بِما حَفِظَ اللَّهُ: in the reading of Abū Jaʿfar [al-Madanī] it is بما حفظ الله with the accusative [i.e. «اللهَ»]. We have mentioned it, but we shall explain it here with careful explanation. The nominative is clearer, i.e. "guarding [the honour of] their absent husbands through Allah's guarding, Mighty and Majestic is He, and His direction"; and it was said: "because of what Allah has secured for them in their dowries and their companionship"; and it was said: "by what Allah has entrusted them to guard, of rendering trusts to their husbands". The accusative means "by the thing that guarded [the command of] Allah", i.e. by the religion or the intellect that guarded Allah's command. And it was said:
"by guarding Allah", i.e. by fear, as in "what you guarded of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He"; and it was said: the implied form is بما حفظن الله ("by their guarding Allah"), then the verb was made singular, as the poet said: [al-Mutaqārib] 97-
فإنّ الحوادث أودى بها
(For the calamities — it destroyed her.)
وَاللَّاتِي تَخافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ: in the position of the nominative by ibtidāʾ (as mubtadaʾ). Its implied form according to the view of Sībawayh is "and among what has been prescribed for you [are those women…]"; according to others the implied form is that the khabar is فَعِظُوهُنَّ. And it was said: «اللاتي» is in the position of the accusative, according to the reading of whoever read وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُما [al-Māʾida: 38] [Translator's note: i.e. the reading with the accusative, «والسارقَ والسارقةَ»]. The view of Abū ʿUbayda and al-Farrāʾ that تخافون means "you are certain" and "you know" is rejected and unknown in the language; تخافون has its usual sense, i.e. you fear that this will come from them because of what has gone before. فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَاهْجُرُوهُنَّ فِي الْمَضاجِعِ: there are three views on it. One of them is that he deserts her in bed, i.e. at the time of sleep. And it was said:
the meaning is "make things plain to them with harsh words and severe rebuke", from their saying أهجر when one speaks obscenely, because Abū Zayd reported هجر and أهجر. The holder of this view said: nushūz is withdrawing from the bed, so how could he desert her in what she has withdrawn from? The third view: Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUbayd, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَاهْجُرُوهُنَّ فِي الْمَضاجِعِ وَاضْرِبُوهُنَّ: he said: all of this is about the matter of the bed; if she returns to the bed, he does not strike her. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the best of what has been said about the verse, i.e. "strike them on account of the beds", as you say هجرت فلانا في الكذب ("I shunned so-and-so on account of lying").

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ شِقاقَ بَيْنِهِما: a condition (sharṭ). فَابْعَثُوا حَكَماً مِنْ أَهْلِهِ وَحَكَماً مِنْ أَهْلِها: its answer (jawāb).
إِنْ يُرِيدا إِصْلاحاً يُوَفِّقِ اللَّهُ بَيْنَهُما: it was said that the two pronouns refer to the two arbiters, because when they want reconciliation they aim at the truth, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, grants them success. And it was said: the two pronouns refer to the spouses, because one is not called an arbiter (ḥakam) unless he wants reconciliation. And it was said: the first pronoun refers to the two arbiters and the second to the spouses.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
وَاعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ: an imperative, which is why the nūn was dropped from it. وَلا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئاً: a prohibition.
وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ إِحْساناً: a maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Farrāʾ said: وبالوالدين إحسان is also allowed, making it nominative by the bāʾ, because the verb is not overt. وَبِذِي الْقُرْبى: genitive by the bāʾ. وَالْيَتامى وَالْمَساكِينِ وَالْجارِ ذِي الْقُرْبى: all conjoined. Al-Farrāʾ said: in the codices of the people of Kufa it is العتق ذا القربى [Translator's note: so in the source; «العتق» appears to be a corruption, probably of «والجار»]; on this basis it must be read والجار ذا القربى, making it accusative by an implied verb and making what follows it accusative. وَالْجارِ الْجُنُبِ وَالصَّاحِبِ بِالْجَنْبِ: al-Akhfash said: al-jār al-junub is the one remote in kinship, i.e. there is no kinship between you and him. He reported والجار الجنب [Translator's note: presumably «الجَنْب», with fatḥa and sukūn; the vowelling is not shown in the source], and recited:
98-
الناس جنب والأمير جنب
(The people are on one side, and the emir is on [another] side.)
Al-janb is the side, i.e. the one who keeps aside from kinship. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I asked Abū Makwaza the Bedouin about al-ṣāḥib bi-l-janb, and he said: "He is the one at your side." Al-Akhfash likewise said: he is the one at your side. One says فلان بجنبك and إلى جنبك. Al-Akhfash reported مفعلة [Translator's note: so in the source; the word is unclear] and والجار الجانب. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I asked Abū Makwaza about al-jār al-junub, and he said: "He is the one who comes and alights wherever [you] alight, on whom your eye falls." وَما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ: in the position of the genitive, i.e. "and do good to what your right hands possess".

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ: in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for «من»; it may be in the position of the nominative as a badal for the latent pronoun in فخور; and it may be in the position of the nominative [as mubtadaʾ], with وَالَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوالَهُمْ رِئاءَ النَّاسِ conjoined to it, and the khabar (predicate) being «إنّ الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرّة», i.e. "He does not wrong them".

nahhas-irab:38-38.t:
وَالَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوالَهُمْ رِئاءَ النَّاسِ: it may be in the position of the nominative, as we mentioned just now; it may be in the position of the accusative, conjoined to الذين when that is a badal (substitute) for من; and it may be in the position of the genitive, conjoined to «الكافرين». وَمَنْ يَكُنِ الشَّيْطانُ لَهُ قَرِيناً: a condition (sharṭ), so dropping the nūn from it is not allowed, because it carries a vowel. As for the meaning, it would be "whoever accepted from Satan in this world, he has become his companion"; and the meaning may be "whoever has Satan joined to him in the Fire". فَساءَ قَرِيناً: accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz, specification), i.e. "evil is Satan as a companion". قرين is of the pattern faʿīl, from joining (iqtirān) and keeping company, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 99-
عن المرء لا تسأل وأبصر قرينه ... فإنّ القرين بالمقارن مقتدي
(Do not ask about a man, but look at his companion, for a companion follows the example of the one he accompanies.)

nahhas-irab:39-39.t:
وَماذا عَلَيْهِمْ: «ما» is in the position of the nominative by ibtidāʾ (as mubtadaʾ), and «وذا» is the khabar (predicate) of «ما», «ذا» meaning:
الذي ("which"); and «ما» and «ذا» may be a single noun.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: وَإِنْ تَكُ حَسَنَةً: the noun (ism) of «تك», which means "occur"; and you may also make حسنة accusative, with the implied form "and if his deed is a good deed". يُضاعِفْها: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). وَيُؤْتِ: conjoined to it. مِنْ لَدُنْهُ: in the position of the genitive by من, except that it is not declined, because it is not fully flexible (lā tatamakkan), whereas «عند» has become flexible, so it takes the accusative and the genitive; its flexibility is that you say هذا القول عندي صواب ("this statement in my view is correct"), but you do not say هذا القول لدي صواب. أَجْراً: a mafʿūl (object). عَظِيماً: its adjective (naʿt).

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: فَكَيْفَ إِذا جِئْنا: the fāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the vowelled letter is presumably the final of كيف, i.e. the fatḥa on the fāʾ at the end of كيف] takes a fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. إِذا: an adverb of time, and what governs it is جِئْنا. وَجِئْنا بِكَ عَلى هؤُلاءِ شَهِيداً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: يَوْمَئِذٍ: an adverb (ẓarf); or, if you wish, it is indeclinable (mabnī). «إذ» is indeclinable and nothing else, and the tanwīn in it is a substitute for what was omitted. وَعَصَوُا الرَّسُولَ: the wāw takes a ḍamma because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and a kasra on it is allowed. لَوْ تُسَوَّى بِهِمُ الْأَرْضُ: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned it. It was also said: its meaning is "if only they were not resurrected", because if they were not resurrected the earth would be level over them, since they were moved [out] from the dust. وَلا يَكْتُمُونَ اللَّهَ حَدِيثاً: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned it, and we mentioned the view of Qatāda that the Resurrection has [different] stations; its meaning is that when it became clear to them and they were brought to account, they did not conceal.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ وَأَنْتُمْ سُكارى حَتَّى: [وأنتم سكارى is] mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). One also says سكارى [Translator's note: presumably the variant vowelling «سَكارى» beside «سُكارى»; the vowels are not shown in the source]; it is a diptote because at its end is the alif of the feminine. حَتَّى تَعْلَمُوا: accusative by حتى. وَلا جُنُباً: conjoined to the position, i.e. "and do not approach prayer while junub (in a state of major ritual impurity)". إِلَّا عابِرِي سَبِيلٍ: accusative as a ḥāl. Al-Akhfash said: as you say لا تأتني إلّا راكبا ("do not come to me except riding"). Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned the meaning of the verse, except that it is one of the difficult [verses] among the rulings of the Qur'an, so we shall add further explanation. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: لا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ وَأَنْتُمْ سُكارى, i.e. [drunk] from sleep. This view is mistaken in several respects: among them, it is not known in the language; the ḥadīth goes against it; and it is not possible for a sleeper to be charged with worship while asleep. So it is established that سكارى is from intoxication, which comes from drinking; and His saying حَتَّى تَعْلَمُوا ما تَقُولُونَ indicates [Translator's note: the source reads «بدل», evidently a corruption of «يدلّ», "indicates"] that whoever knows what he is saying is not drunk. وَلا جُنُباً إِلَّا عابِرِي سَبِيلٍ: there are two views on it:
One of them is that the meaning is "do not pray when you have become junub" — one says أجنبتم, جنبتم and جنبتم [Translator's note: the vowel distinctions between the last two forms are not shown in the source] — إِلَّا عابِرِي سَبِيلٍ, "except when travelling", so you perform tayammum (dry ablution) and pray. On this basis it follows that the junub may not perform tayammum unless he is a traveller. This is the view of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah have mercy on him. The other view: لا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ means "do not approach the place of prayer", which is the mosque, «إلّا عابري سبيل», "except passing through", as ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said — [someone asked:] "May the junub step through the mosque?"
He said: "Yes; do you not recite «إلّا عابري سبيل»?" This is the position of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, Ibn ʿAbbās and Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah have mercy on them: that the junub may perform tayammum when resident. وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضى: i.e. sick with an illness on account of which you cannot reach for water, or you fear perishing from cold or wounds.
أَوْ عَلى سَفَرٍ: in which you do not find water. أَوْ جاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ مِنَ الْغائِطِ: we have mentioned that one of the jurists said: «أو» means the wāw ("and"); he needed this only because illness and travel are not ritual impurities (ḥadath), while relieving oneself is a ḥadath. The skilled among the scholars of Arabic do not allow «أو» to mean the wāw, because they differ [in meaning]. Some of them say: in the speech there is placing earlier and later (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), and the implied form is «لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى، أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط، أو لامستم النساء، وإن كنتم جنبا فاطهّروا» ("do not approach prayer while drunk, or [if] one of you has come from relieving himself, or you have touched women; and if you are junub, then purify yourselves"), i.e. "and if you are junub and wish to pray". Placing earlier and later is not to be denied, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَكانَ لِزاماً وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى [Ṭā Hā: 129], i.e. "were it not for a word that preceded from your Lord and an appointed term"; and Imruʾ al-Qays said: [al-Ṭawīl] 100-
فلو أن ما أسعى لأدنى معيشة ... كفاني ولم أطلب قليل من المال
(Had I been striving for the meanest living, a little wealth would have sufficed me and I would not have sought [more].)
And it was said: there is an omission in the speech without placing earlier and later, and the meaning is: "and if you are sick or on a journey and you have risen to pray in a state of ritual impurity, then perform tayammum with clean earth"; likewise يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلاةِ [al-Māʾida: 6] means "when you rise in a state of ritual impurity". أَوْ لامَسْتُمُ النِّساءَ: there are three views on its meaning: one, that لمستم means "you had intercourse"; one, that لمستم means "you had skin contact"; and one, that لمستم combines both matters. لامستم has its meaning according to most people, except that it is reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he said: the more appropriate in the language is that لامستم means "you kissed" or the like, because each of the two has an action [in it]; and he said: لمستم means "you covered [them]" and "you touched", and the woman has no action in this. إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَفُوًّا: i.e. He accepts al-ʿafw, which is what is easy. غَفُوراً: of sins. The meaning of "Allah forgave (ghafara) his sin" is that He veiled its punishment from him and did not punish him.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: أَلَمْ تَرَ: the alif was dropped for the jussive; the original has a hamza, which was dropped for lightness. إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيباً مِنَ الْكِتابِ يَشْتَرُونَ الضَّلالَةَ: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا السَّبِيلَ: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِأَعْدائِكُمْ: it is related of al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAmr that they assimilated the mīm into the bāʾ. That is not allowed, because the mīm has nasalisation (ghunna), and if you assimilated it, it would be lost. وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); it was added because the meaning is "be content with Allah". وَلِيًّا: as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz, specification), or, if you wish, as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and likewise وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ نَصِيراً.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t:
مِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ عَنْ مَواضِعِهِ: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and al-Nakhaʿī read يحرّفون الكلام عن مواضعه. Abū Jaʿfar said: الكلم is more appropriate here, because they only distort the words of the Prophet ﷺ or what they have in the Torah; they do not distort all speech. The meaning of يحرفون is that they interpret otherwise than its [true] interpretation; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, censured them for that because they do it deliberately.
وَاسْمَعْ غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍ: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned the view of Ibn ʿAbbās that its meaning is "may you not hear", and its explanation is "hear — may you not hear". This is what they intend, while they make it appear that they mean "hear, without being made to hear anything disagreeable or hurtful". As for the view of al-Ḥasan that its meaning is "not heard from you", i.e. not responded to in what you say — if it were so, the wording would have been غير مسموع منك. وَراعِنا: al-Akhfash said: i.e. "lend us your hearing", i.e. "attend to us". It was also said: by their saying وراعنا they meant "and pasture our livestock", in mockery of addressing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Abū Jaʿfar said: the explanation of this — and Allah knows best — is that by their saying راعنا they make it appear [that they mean] "lend us your hearing", while they intend al-murāʿāh [Translator's note: so in the source]. This is indicated by His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, لَيًّا بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ وَطَعْناً فِي الدِّينِ, i.e. they twist their tongues, i.e. incline them towards what is in their hearts, and they attack the religion, i.e. they say to their companions: "If he were a prophet, he would know that we are insulting him." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made the Prophet ﷺ aware of that, and it was one of the signs of his prophethood; and He forbade them this saying. لَيًّا: a maṣdar (verbal noun), or, if you wish, a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); its original form is لويا, then the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ. وَطَعْناً: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ قالُوا سَمِعْنا وَأَطَعْنا: «أنّ» is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "if this had occurred". And it was said: «إنّ» [Translator's note: so in the source; «أنّ» is meant] has come in the position of the verb only because there must be a clause after it.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: مُصَدِّقاً لِما مَعَكُمْ: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَطْمِسَ وُجُوهاً: one also says نطمس [Translator's note: presumably «نَطْمُسَ», with ḍamma; the vowels are not shown in the source]; and in ordinary speech one says طسم, يطسم and يطسم with the meaning of طمس. وَكانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ مَفْعُولًا: the noun of كان and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:48-48.t:
إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned it, and we shall add further clarification. This is of the unambiguous (muḥkam); وَيَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ is of the ambiguous (mutashābih) about which the scholars have spoken. Some of them said: this was ambiguous until Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made it clear by the threat [of punishment]. Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said: «This verse has made clear that every person who commits a major sin is subject to the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: if He wills, He pardons his sin, and if He wills, He punishes him for it, so long as his major sin is not associating partners with Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.» And some of them said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has made it clear by His saying إِنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبائِرَ ما تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئاتِكُمْ [al-Nisāʾ: 31], informing [us] that He wills to forgive the minor sins of whoever avoids the major sins, and does not forgive them for whoever commits major sins. A third view is that the meaning of «لمن يشاء» is "for whoever repents", and it is a statement after a statement that He forgives associating partners and all sins for whoever repents. «فأن» [Translator's note: i.e. أن in أن يشرك] is in the position of the accusative by يغفر. It may also be in the position of the accusative in the sense that Allah does not forgive a sin together with associating partners with Him, and [in the sense of] "for associating partners with Him" (وبأن يشرك به); and according to the school of a group of grammarians, on this answer, «أن» may be in the position of the genitive. وَمَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ: a condition (sharṭ), and its answer is فَقَدِ افْتَرى إِثْماً عَظِيماً, i.e. he fabricated. From it is افترى فلان على فلان, i.e. he accused him of what was not in him; and فريت الشيء means "I cut the thing".

nahhas-irab:49-50.t: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ بَلِ اللَّهُ يُزَكِّي مَنْ يَشاءُ: i.e. He names him obedient and a friend [of Allah]. Then He made the Prophet ﷺ marvel at that, saying: انْظُرْ كَيْفَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ, in their saying "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved ones" — and this is the self-purification. وَكَفى بِهِ إِثْماً مُبِيناً: as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz, specification).

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيباً مِنَ الْكِتابِ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْجِبْتِ وَالطَّاغُوتِ: these two are everything worshipped apart from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. Their believing in al-jibt and al-ṭāghūt is their saying to those who worshipped idols: هؤُلاءِ أَهْدى than the monotheist believers. The view of Ibn ʿAbbās that al-jibt and al-ṭāghūt are Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab is not outside that; it is only by way of likening the two of them to al-jibt and al-ṭāghūt, because they obeyed the two of them in denying the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. سَبِيلًا: as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz, specification).

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:53-53.t:
أَمْ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُلْكِ: because they disdained following the Prophet ﷺ. The implied form is: "Are they more entitled to prophethood than the one I sent, or do they have a share of the kingdom?" This omission is indicated by أم coming at the beginning of the speech, because it is known that before it something has been omitted. فَإِذاً لا يُؤْتُونَ النَّاسَ نَقِيراً: i.e. they withhold rights; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed [us] of what He knows of them. Sībawayh said: «إذن» among the governors of verbs is like أظنّ among the governors of nouns, i.e. it is made inoperative when the speech does not rest upon it. If it is at the beginning of the speech and what follows it is future, it governs the accusative and nothing else; if a fāʾ or a wāw precedes it, both the nominative and the accusative occur: the nominative on the basis that the fāʾ is attached to the verb, and the accusative on the basis that the fāʾ is attached to إذن. On this basis, outside the Qur'an, فإذن لا يؤتوا الناس نقيرا is allowed. What governs the verb in the accusative according to Sībawayh is «إذا» [Translator's note: so in the source; «إذن» is meant], because of its resemblance to أن.
What governs it in the accusative according to al-Khalīl is an implied «أن» after إذن; according to him, a verb is made accusative only by أن, overt or implied. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that إذن is written with an alif and that it takes tanwīn. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: "I would like to brand the hand of whoever writes إذن with an alif, because it is like «لن» and «أن», and tanwīn does not enter particles."

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: أَمْ يَحْسُدُونَ النَّاسَ عَلى ما آتاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ: because they envied the Prophet ﷺ. فَقَدْ آتَيْنا آلَ إِبْراهِيمَ الْكِتابَ: i.e. they acknowledge this, so why do they envy one whom Allah has favoured with it?

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ آمَنَ بِهِ: [i.e.] in the Prophet ﷺ, because he has been mentioned before and he is the one envied. It may also be that به refers to the Qur'an, because it has been mentioned before; and it may be that به refers to the Book. وَكَفى بِجَهَنَّمَ سَعِيراً: i.e. for whoever turned away from him. سعير is in the sense of مسعورة ("kindled").

nahhas-irab:56-56.t:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِنا: the noun (ism) of «إنّ», and the khabar (predicate) is سَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِمْ ناراً. كُلَّما: an adverb (ẓarf).
نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُمْ: [read] with assimilation, because the tāʾ is from the tip of the tongue and the jīm from its middle; and pronouncing it distinctly is better so that the jīms do not come together [Translator's note: so in the source]. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned two views on its meaning which come back to a single meaning, namely that the meaning is: "We restore the cooked [skin] as uncooked", and the pain falls only on the soul, because it is what feels and perceives. Similar to it is كُلَّما خَبَتْ زِدْناهُمْ سَعِيراً [al-Isrāʾ: 97], i.e. He restores the cooked as uncooked so that the fire blazes; as one says تبدّلت بعدنا, i.e. "you have changed [since we left]". لِيَذُوقُوا: accusative by the lām of kay (purpose), which is a substitute for «أن».
إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَزِيزاً: i.e. nothing is beyond His power and nothing escapes Him. حَكِيماً: in His threatening His servants and in all His acts.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t:
وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ: the position of الذين is accusative, by conjunction (ʿaṭf) according to what the wording requires; or, if you wish, it is nominative, and that is better, on the [basis of the] position; or, if you wish, as mubtadaʾ (subject). الذين:
is not declined, because if it were declined it would be declined in the middle of the noun; and it was said: because it is used only for one absent. The nūn takes a fatḥa because it is a plural; and it was said: because a yāʾ precedes it; and it was said: because it is like one thing joined to another. There are several dialectal forms of it: the form with which the Qur'an came is «الذين» in the nominative, genitive and accusative positions. The Banū Kināna say الذون in the nominative position. Some of the Arabs say اللاذون in the nominative and genitive positions [Translator's note: so in the source], and some say اللذيّون. In the dual there are also four forms: one says اللذان with the nūn light, and اللذانّ with it doubled — doubled as compensation for what was omitted, and it was said: to distinguish it from what is dropped in annexation; one says اللّذيّان with the yāʾ doubled; and one says اللّذا without nūn. Sībawayh recited: [al-Kāmil] 101-
أبني كليب إنّ عمّيّ اللّذا ... قتلا الملوك وفكّكا الأغلالا
(O sons of Kulayb, my two paternal uncles are the ones who killed the kings and broke the fetters.)
In the singular there are several forms: one says جاءني الذي كلّمك, and جاءني اللذ كلمك with the dhāl taking kasra, without yāʾ, and اللّذ with the dhāl quiescent, as the poet said:
102-
كاللّذ تزبّى زيبة فاصطيدا
(Like the one who went down into a pit [dug to trap game] and was himself caught.)
One also says الذيّ with the yāʾ doubled. Ṭayyiʾ say جاءني ذو قال ذاك, with the wāw, and رأيت ذو قال ذاك and مررت بذو قال ذاك, in the sense of الذي. سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ: two objects (mafʿūlān); the doctrine of Sībawayh is that the implied form is "into gardens" (في جنّات), with «في» omitted. تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ: an adjective (naʿt) of جنات. خالِدِينَ: also an adjective, because the reference [pronoun] has come back [to them]; or, if you wish, it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
أَبَداً: an adverb of time.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t:
إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ: an imperfect (future) verb; making the rāʾ quiescent is a solecism (laḥn). أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا: in the position of the accusative.
The original is بأن تؤدّوا. The maṣdar (verbal noun) is تأدية, and the noun is الأداء. We have mentioned نِعِمَّا in «Sūrat al-Baqara».

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: ذلِكَ خَيْرٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). وَأَحْسَنُ: conjoined to خير. تَأْوِيلًا: as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz, specification).

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: يُرِيدُونَ: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). أَنْ يَتَحاكَمُوا: a mafʿūl (object). إِلَى الطَّاغُوتِ: we have mentioned the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk that it means Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf; according to the philologists this is everything worshipped apart from Allah. It is related that their seeking judgement from al-ṭāghūt was that they used to cast divining arrows, and when the arrow on which was written "do" or "do not do" came out, they said: "al-ṭāghūt has judged this for us"; they did this before the idols. وَيُرِيدُ الشَّيْطانُ أَنْ يُضِلَّهُمْ: i.e. by that. ضَلالًا بَعِيداً: construed according to the sense, i.e. "so they go astray a far straying"; and similar to it is وَاللَّهُ أَنْبَتَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ نَباتاً (17) [Nūḥ: 17].

nahhas-irab:61-61.t: يَصُدُّونَ عَنْكَ صُدُوداً: a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar) according to al-Khalīl, the maṣdar being الصدّ; the Kufans say: both are maṣdars (verbal nouns).

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: فَكَيْفَ إِذا أَصابَتْهُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ: i.e. from no longer seeking their help and from the humiliation that befalls them, as in فَقُلْ لَنْ تَخْرُجُوا مَعِيَ أَبَداً وَلَنْ تُقاتِلُوا مَعِيَ عَدُوًّا [al-Tawba: 83]. ثُمَّ جاؤُكَ يَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ: a ḥāl (circumstantial). إِنْ أَرَدْنا إِلَّا إِحْساناً: «إن» means «ما» ("not").

nahhas-irab:63-63.t: أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ ما فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ: i.e. do not accept their excuse. وَعِظْهُمْ: make them fear the punishment. وَقُلْ لَهُمْ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ قَوْلًا بَلِيغاً: i.e. of the threat, one that reaches deep into them. One says بلغ الرجل بلاغة ("the man became eloquent"), and رجل بليغ is one who reaches with his tongue the essence of what is in his heart. The Arabs say أحمق بلغ and بلغ, i.e. the utmost in foolishness; and it was said: its meaning is "he attains what he wants, even though he is a fool".

nahhas-irab:64-64.t: وَما أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا لِيُطاعَ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ: «من» is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis. وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ إِذْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ: «أنّ» is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "if this had occurred". لَوَجَدُوا اللَّهَ تَوَّاباً رَحِيماً: i.e. accepting their repentance; these two are objects (mafʿūlān) and nothing else.

nahhas-irab:65-65.t:
فَلا وَرَبِّكَ: genitive by the wāw of the oath, which is a substitute for the bāʾ because of its resemblance to it. The answer of the oath is لا يُؤْمِنُونَ. حَتَّى يُحَكِّمُوكَ: accusative by حتى, and the sign of the accusative is the dropping of the nūn. Abū al-Sammāl read
فِيما شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ with the jīm quiescent; this is a solecism (laḥn) according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh: according to them the fatḥa is not dropped, because of its lightness. ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr related it from his brother ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, who said: a man of the Anṣār disputed with me before the Prophet ﷺ over water from which we all used to irrigate, and the Prophet ﷺ said: «اسق يا زبير ثم خلّ لجارك، فقال الأنصاريّ: يا رسول الله أن كان ابن عمّتك. فتلوّن وجه النبي صلّى الله عليه وسلّم» ("Irrigate, O Zubayr, then let [the water] go to your neighbour." The Anṣārī said: "O Messenger of Allah, [is it] because he is your paternal aunt's son?" And the face of the Prophet ﷺ changed colour). Al-Zubayr said: I do not think this verse was revealed except about him: فَلا وَرَبِّكَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ حَتَّى يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيما شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ. By another chain [it is related] that the Anṣārī was Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa [Translator's note: the source prints «أب بلتعة»].

nahhas-irab:66-66.t: وَلَوْ أَنَّا كَتَبْنا عَلَيْهِمْ أَنِ اقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ: you give the nūn a ḍamma because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the ḍamma was chosen because the tāʾ has a ḍamma; or, if you wish, you give it a kasra according to the basic rule; and likewise أَوِ اخْرُجُوا مِنْ دِيارِكُمْ. ما فَعَلُوهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ: as a badal (substitute) for the wāw. The people of Kufa say: by repetition (takrīr): "they did not do it — none did it but a few of them". ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read ما فعلوه إلّا قليلا منهم, in the accusative as the excepted. The nominative is better according to all the grammarians; the nominative became better only because the wording takes precedence over the meaning, and it [also] includes the meaning. وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ فَعَلُوا ما يُوعَظُونَ بِهِ لَكانَ خَيْراً لَهُمْ: i.e. in this world and the Hereafter. وَأَشَدَّ تَثْبِيتاً: in their affairs; «تثبيتا» is as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz, specification).

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: I.e. a reward in the Hereafter.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ: a condition (sharṭ), and the answer is فَأُولئِكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ. وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ: the followers of the prophets. وَالشُّهَداءِ: those who upheld justice and bore witness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, with the truth; and it was said: those killed in the way of Allah. And it was said: the one killed is called shahīd only because he bore witness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, with the truth and upheld his testimony until he was killed; and it was said: because he witnessed the honour of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. There is a third view on it: that he will bear witness against the servants concerning their deeds on the Day of Resurrection; and it is said that the martyrs will be upright witnesses on the Day of Resurrection. Abū al-Sammāl al-ʿAdawī read وَحَسُنَ أُولئِكَ رَفِيقاً [Translator's note: presumably with the sīn quiescent, «وحَسْنَ», since the following remark concerns transferring the ḍamma; the vowelling of the source does not show the difference]. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is allowed by the transfer of the ḍamma. Al-Akhfash said: «رفيقا» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it means "companions" (رفقاء). The Kufans said: it is accusative as tafsīr (specification, i.e. tamyīz), because the Arabs say حسن أولئك من رفقاء ("how good are those as companions") and كرم زيد من رجل ("how noble is Zayd as a man"), and the entry of «من» indicates that it explains that verb.

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: ذلِكَ الْفَضْلُ مِنَ اللَّهِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. that immense reward is a bounty from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, because He had bestowed favour on them in this world; it could have been that that bliss was [due] to their deeds. In the ḥadīth: «لا يدخل الجنة أحد بعمله» ("No one will enter Paradise by his deed"). There are two answers about it: one of them is this, and that it is like the verse; and the other answer is that they had sins, and it could have been that the deeds were made recompense for the sins.

nahhas-irab:71-71.t: فَانْفِرُوا ثُباتٍ: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The singular is ثبة. The middle of a water-basin is also called ثبة, and one weak in Arabic may imagine that they are one [word] and that one of them is from the other, but there is a difference between them: for ثبة of the basin one says, in the diminutive, ثويبة, because it is from ثاب يثوب, and for ثبة meaning a group one says ثبيّة. أَوِ انْفِرُوا جَمِيعاً: accusative as a ḥāl according to Sībawayh.

nahhas-irab:72-72.t:
وَإِنَّ مِنْكُمْ لَمَنْ لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ: the first lām is the lām of emphasis, and the second is the lām of the oath. «من» is in the position of the accusative, and its ṣila (relative clause) is لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ, because it has the sense of an oath; the khabar (predicate) is مِنْكُمْ. Mujāhid read وَإِنَّ مِنْكُمْ لَمَنْ لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ [Translator's note: printed identically in the source; Mujāhid's reading is reported as «لَيُبْطِئَنَّ»]. فَإِنْ أَصابَتْكُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ قالَ قَدْ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيَّ: it came in the singular according to the wording; had it been قالوا, it would have been allowed; and likewise throughout the verse.
Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Ḥafṣ read [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off here in the source; it evidently refers to the reading «كأن لم تكن» with tāʾ in the next verse].

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: كَأَنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُ مَوَدَّةٌ: whoever uses the masculine [يكن] takes مودة in the sense of الودّ. فَأَفُوزَ فَوْزاً عَظِيماً: the answer to the wish (jawāb al-tamannī).

nahhas-irab:74-74.t: فَلْيُقاتِلْ: an imperative; the kasra was dropped from the lām for lightness. الَّذِينَ يَشْرُونَ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا بِالْآخِرَةِ: we have mentioned that the meaning of يشترون [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «يَشْرُونَ»] is "they sell", i.e. they give up their lives and wealth for Allah. بِالْآخِرَةِ: i.e. for the reward of the Hereafter. وَمَنْ يُقاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: a condition (sharṭ). فَيُقْتَلْ أَوْ يَغْلِبْ: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. And the requital is فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أَجْراً عَظِيماً.

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: وَما لَكُمْ لا تُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: in the position of the accusative [as a ḥāl], as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: فَما لَهُمْ عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ [al-Muddaththir: 49]. وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: I prefer that the meaning be "on behalf of (في) the oppressed", because the two ways are different, as though the way of the oppressed were their deliverance. Abū Isḥāq said: rather, the preferred [view] is that the meaning be "and in the way of the oppressed", for the deliverance of the oppressed is part of the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ: an adjective (naʿt) of المستضعفين; and it may be an adjective of all those made genitive by من. مِنْ هذِهِ الْقَرْيَةِ الظَّالِمِ أَهْلُها: an adjective of القرية, even though the act belongs to the pronoun [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. to what follows], as you say مررت بالرجل العاقل أبوه ("I passed by the man whose father is wise"). It did not say الظالمين, because it is an adjective standing in place of a verb, i.e. "whose people have done wrong". وَاجْعَلْ لَنا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ وَلِيًّا: i.e. one who rescues us from them. وَاجْعَلْ لَنا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ نَصِيراً: i.e. one who helps us against them.

nahhas-irab:76-76.t:
الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: a mubtadaʾ (subject). يُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: an imperfect verb in the position of the khabar (predicate); and likewise وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ الطَّاغُوتِ. Abū ʿUbayda and al-Kisāʾī said: الطاغوت is masculine and feminine.
Abū ʿUbayda said: it is masculine and feminine only because they used to call the male soothsayer and the female soothsayer ṭāghūt. He said:
Ḥajjāj related to us from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abū al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh when he was asked about the ṭawāghīt (al-ṭāghūt) to which they used to go for judgement, and he said: "There was one among Juhayna, one among Aslam, and one in every tribe." Abū Isḥāq said: the proof that it is Satan is His saying فَقاتِلُوا أَوْلِياءَ الشَّيْطانِ إِنَّ كَيْدَ الشَّيْطانِ كانَ ضَعِيفاً.

nahhas-irab:77-77.t: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ قِيلَ لَهُمْ كُفُّوا أَيْدِيَكُمْ: it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that some people wished for fighting before permission was given for it, and the Prophet ﷺ forbade them; then when it was prescribed they disliked it, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ قِيلَ لَهُمْ كُفُّوا أَيْدِيَكُمْ ... to its end. يَخْشَوْنَ النَّاسَ كَخَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). أَوْ أَشَدَّ: conjoined to the kāf, in the position of the accusative; and it may be conjoined to خشية, in the position of the genitive. كَخَشْيَةِ [Translator's note: so in the source; the word meant is evidently «خَشْيَةً» after أشدّ]: as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz, specification). لِمَ كَتَبْتَ عَلَيْنَا الْقِتالَ: the original is «لما»; the alif was dropped because it is interrogative. لَوْلا أَخَّرْتَنا إِلى أَجَلٍ: i.e. "why not" (هلّا), and only a verb follows it. قُلْ مَتاعُ الدُّنْيا قَلِيلٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); and likewise وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لِمَنِ اتَّقى, i.e. who guarded against acts of disobedience.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t: أَيْنَما تَكُونُوا يُدْرِكْكُمُ الْمَوْتُ وَلَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُرُوجٍ مُشَيَّدَةٍ وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ حَسَنَةٌ يَقُولُوا هذِهِ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَقُولُوا هذِهِ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ قُلْ كُلٌّ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ فَمالِ هؤُلاءِ الْقَوْمِ لا يَكادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ حَدِيثاً (78) أَيْنَما تَكُونُوا يُدْرِكْكُمُ الْمَوْتُ: a condition and requital (sharṭ and mujāzāh), and «ما» is redundant (zāʾida). وَلَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُرُوجٍ مُشَيَّدَةٍ: [the doubled form] for intensification (taktīr). One says شاد البنيان ("he erected the building") and أشاد بذكره ("he spread his fame"). وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ حَسَنَةٌ يَقُولُوا هذِهِ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ: a condition and requital; and likewise وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَقُولُوا هذِهِ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ. قُلْ كُلٌّ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). فَمالِ هؤُلاءِ الْقَوْمِ لا يَكادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ حَدِيثاً: i.e. they do not know its meaning and its interpretation; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, had made it clear to them, saying: حَتَّى إِذا فَشِلْتُمْ وَتَنازَعْتُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ [Āl ʿImrān: 152]. The lām is joined [in writing] according to the Basrans and al-Farrāʾ, because it is a lām of the genitive; and Ibn Saʿdān reported its being separated.

nahhas-irab:79-79.t: ما أَصابَكَ مِنْ حَسَنَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ وَما أَصابَكَ مِنْ سَيِّئَةٍ فَمِنْ نَفْسِكَ: al-Akhfash said: «ما» means "that which" (الذي); and it was said: it is conditional. The correct view is that of al-Akhfash, because it was revealed concerning a specific thing, namely drought, and this has nothing to do with acts of disobedience; had it been about them, it would have been وما أصبت من سيئة ("whatever evil you committed"). Mujāhid related from Ibn ʿAbbās: «ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك» وأنا كتبتها عليك ("…and I decreed it for you"); this is a reading by way of explanation (tafsīr). وَأَرْسَلْناكَ لِلنَّاسِ رَسُولًا: an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun) [Translator's note: i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object]; and the meaning may be "possessing a message". وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً: as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz, specification).

nahhas-irab:81-81.t: وَيَقُولُونَ طاعَةٌ: i.e. "our affair is obedience" or "from us is obedience". Al-Akhfash said: طاعة in the accusative is allowed, i.e. "we obey with obedience". بَيَّتَ طائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ: He made الطائفة masculine because in meaning they are men. The Kufans assimilated the tāʾ into the ṭāʾ because they are from one point of articulation; al-Kisāʾī considered that ugly in the verb, while according to the Basrans it is not ugly, and it is the reading of Abū ʿAmr. فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ: an imperative, i.e. trust in Him. وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا: i.e. as a helper for you against your enemy and one in whom trust is placed.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: أَفَلا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ: i.e. do they not look into its outcome (ʿāqiba)? In the ḥadīth: «لا تدابروا» [Translator's note: printed «لا تدبروا» in the source], i.e. let not some of you turn your backs (dubur) on others; and أدبر القوم means their affair has gone on to its end. By this He indicated that reflecting upon the Qur'an is obligatory so that its meaning may be known; and in this there is a refutation of whoever said: the interpretation of the Qur'an is to be taken only from the Prophet ﷺ. ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا: because there is no speaker who speaks a great deal without much inconsistency being found in his speech, whether in description and wording, or in excellence of meaning, or in contradiction, or in falsehood. So He, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed the Qur'an and commanded reflection upon it, because they do not find in it any inconsistency in a description of defects, nor baseness in a meaning, nor contradiction, nor falsehood in what they are told of knowledge of the unseen, of what they conceal.

nahhas-irab:83-83.t: وَإِذا جاءَهُمْ أَمْرٌ مِنَ الْأَمْنِ: إذا has the sense of a condition, but it is not used to govern a requital [in the jussive]. The meaning is that when they heard anything of affairs involving security, such as the victory of the Muslims and the killing of their enemy. أَوِ الْخَوْفِ: which is the opposite of this. أَذاعُوا بِهِ: i.e. they made it public and talked about it before they had ascertained its truth; so they were forbidden that, because of the lying and rumour-mongering that it brings upon them. وَلَوْ رَدُّوهُ إِلَى الرَّسُولِ وَإِلى أُولِي الْأَمْرِ مِنْهُمْ: and they are the commanders. لَعَلِمَهُ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَنْبِطُونَهُ مِنْهُمْ: i.e. they extract it by questioning.
