This is derived from «النبط», which is the first water that comes out of a well when it is first dug; the Nabaṭ (Nabataeans) were called Nabaṭ because they extract what is in the ground. وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ: nominative by ibtidāʾ (as mubtadaʾ), with the khabar [omitted] according to Sībawayh, and according to him the khabar may not be made overt; the Kufans say: nominative by لولا. لَاتَّبَعْتُمُ الشَّيْطانَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا: there are three views on this verse. Abū ʿUbayd said: the implied form is "they spread it, except a few"; this is the view of a group of grammarians, who said: because most of those who investigate do not know. Abū Isḥāq said: rather, the implied form is «لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم إلا قليلا» ("those of them who investigate it would have known it, except a few"), because most [people] know this investigation, since it is seeking knowledge through a report. These two are views based on figurative construction (majāz), and a third view is without figurative construction: the meaning would be "were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, in that He sent among you a messenger who established the proof among you, you would have disbelieved and associated partners [with Allah], except a few of you", i.e. that he used to profess the unity of Allah.

nahhas-irab:84-84.t: فَقاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: this fāʾ is connected to His saying وَمَنْ يُقاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَيُقْتَلْ أَوْ يَغْلِبْ فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أَجْراً عَظِيماً [al-Nisāʾ: 74]: "so fight in the way of Allah", i.e. for the sake of this, fight. It may also be connected to His saying وَما لَكُمْ لا تُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ [al-Nisāʾ: 75]. لا تُكَلَّفُ: nominative, because it is an imperfect verb; it is not jussive because it is not a consequence of the first. Al-Akhfash claimed that its jussive is allowed. إِلَّا نَفْسَكَ: the khabar [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. the second object] of the verb whose agent is not named. عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَكُفَّ بَأْسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: an arousing of hope (iṭmāʿ), and arousing of hope from Allah, Glorified is He, is binding, given that hope (al-ṭamaʿ) has come in the speech of the Arabs in the sense of necessity; and it has been said that from it is وَالَّذِي أَطْمَعُ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ لِي خَطِيئَتِي يَوْمَ الدِّينِ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 82]. وَاللَّهُ أَشَدُّ بَأْساً: accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz, specification); and likewise وَأَشَدُّ تَنْكِيلًا.

nahhas-irab:85-85.t:
مَنْ يَشْفَعْ شَفاعَةً حَسَنَةً يَكُنْ لَهُ نَصِيبٌ مِنْها: al-Ḥasan said: whoever intercedes in something has a reward even if his intercession is not accepted, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said «من يشفع» and did not say من يشفع [Translator's note: the second is evidently «يُشَفَّع», "whose intercession is accepted"; the source does not show the difference]. In the ḥadīth: «اشفعوا تؤجروا» ("Intercede and you will be rewarded"), and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, decrees on the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ whatever He wills. It is related that this was revealed concerning the Jews: they used to invoke destruction upon the Muslims in their absence, and in their presence to say "al-sām ʿalaykum" [Translator's note: the source prints «السلام عليكم»; the well-known report has «السام عليكم», "death be upon you"]. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed مَنْ يَشْفَعْ شَفاعَةً حَسَنَةً يَكُنْ لَهُ نَصِيبٌ مِنْها وَمَنْ يَشْفَعْ شَفاعَةً سَيِّئَةً يَكُنْ لَهُ كِفْلٌ مِنْها, and followed that with His saying وَإِذا حُيِّيتُمْ بِتَحِيَّةٍ, which is the greeting of peace.
Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī said: «الكفل» is the share. Al-Kisāʾī said: the origin of al-kifl is a saddle-pad prepared on the back of a camel; and this is a good view. One says اكتفلت البعير when you wrap a cloth around a place on its back and then ride the camel; so you have taken only a share of the camel. وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُقِيتاً: the noun of كان and its khabar (predicate). Abū ʿUbayda said: «المقيت» is the guardian; al-Kisāʾī said: al-muqīt is the all-powerful. The view of Abū ʿUbayda is more appropriate, because it is derived from al-qūt (sustenance), and al-qūt means the amount that preserves a person.

nahhas-irab:86-86.t:
وَإِذا حُيِّيتُمْ بِتَحِيَّةٍ فَحَيُّوا بِأَحْسَنَ مِنْها: it is a diptote because it is of the pattern afʿal and is an adjective, i.e. "with a greeting better than it". Ibn ʿAbbās said: if he says "Salām ʿalaykum", you say "Wa-ʿalaykum al-salām wa-raḥmatu Allāh wa-barakātuh", and this is better than it. أَوْ رُدُّوها: [i.e.] "and upon you" (وعليكم), and this is for the disbelievers — he means the second [clause]. Someone else said:
it is not allowed to say to the disbelievers "Wa-ʿalaykum al-salām", just as it is not allowed to ask mercy for their dead or their living. إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَسِيباً: it was said: "one who takes account", as one says أكيل in the sense of مواكل ("one who eats with another"). Mujāhid said: «حسيبا» means "guarding"; Abū ʿUbayda said: "sufficing". Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the clearest of them. One says:
أحسبني الشيء, i.e. "the thing sufficed me", and from it is حَسْبَكَ اللَّهُ [al-Anfāl: 64]. And I have shown that this is a mistake in the other book [Translator's note: so in the source; the statement appears to contradict the preceding preference and may be corrupt].

nahhas-irab:87-87.t: اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ: [it is called the Day of al-Qiyāma] because people stand (yaqūmūn) in it before the Lord of the worlds, Mighty and Majestic is He; and it was said: because people rise from their graves to it. وَمَنْ أَصْدَقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ حَدِيثاً: as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz, specification).

nahhas-irab:88-88.t:
فَما لَكُمْ فِي الْمُنافِقِينَ فِئَتَيْنِ: Shuʿba related from ʿAdī ibn Thābit, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd, from Zayd ibn Thābit, who said: some men stayed behind from Uḥud, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ differed about them: one group said "Kill them" and another group said "Pardon them". So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed فَما لَكُمْ فِي الْمُنافِقِينَ فِئَتَيْنِ.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: these were people who stayed behind in Mecca and professed Islam to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: "If Muḥammad prevails, we have acknowledged [him]; and if our people prevail, that is dearer to us." So the Muslims became two groups concerning them: some took them as allies, and some disowned them. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said فَما لَكُمْ فِي الْمُنافِقِينَ فِئَتَيْنِ وَاللَّهُ أَرْكَسَهُمْ بِما كَسَبُوا; thus Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made clear their disbelief and made disavowal of them obligatory. Al-Akhfash said: «فئتين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), as one says مالك قائما ("why are you standing?"). The Kufans said: it is the khabar of ما لكم, like the khabar of كان and ظننت, and they allowed the definite article to be brought into it. Al-Farrāʾ reported: أركسهم, i.e. He returned them to disbelief. Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. He returned them to the status of the disbelievers. أَتُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَهْدُوا مَنْ أَضَلَّ اللَّهُ: i.e. that you guide him to the reward by having the rulings of the believers applied to him. فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ سَبِيلًا: i.e. to [any] argument.

nahhas-irab:90-90.t: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ: an exception from وَاقْتُلُوهُمْ. It is related that these were people who were connected to the Banū Mudlij, who were at peace with the Prophet ﷺ. «يصلون», i.e. they are connected. أَوْ جاؤُكُمْ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ: i.e. [their breasts] are constricted. The grammarians have four views on it in this form: al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. "their breasts having become constricted" (قد حصرت), with «قد» implied. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: it is an imprecation, as you say لعن الله الكافرين ("may Allah curse the disbelievers"). And it was said: it is a khabar after a khabar. The fourth view is that حصرت is in the position of the genitive as an adjective (naʿt) of قوم. In the text (ḥarf) of Ubayy: إلا الذين يصلون إلى قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق حصرت صدورهم, without أَوْ جاؤُكُمْ. Al-Ḥasan read أو جاؤكم حصرة صدورهم, in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); its genitive as an adjective is allowed, and its nominative as mubtadaʾ and khabar. أو جاؤكم حصرات صدورهم was also reported, and the nominative is allowed. يُقاتِلُوكُمْ: in the position of the accusative, i.e. "from fighting you" (من أن يقاتلوكم).

nahhas-irab:91-91.t: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read كلّما ردّوا إلى الفتنة with a kasra on the rāʾ [i.e. «رِدُّوا»], because the original is رددوا; it was assimilated and the kasra was shifted onto the rāʾ. Similar to it is وَإِذَا الْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ [al-Inshiqāq: 3] and وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّها وَحُقَّتْ [al-Inshiqāq: 2]. فَإِنْ لَمْ يَعْتَزِلُوكُمْ: إن has come upon لم because the meaning is that of a past verb: "if they do not withdraw from fighting you", i.e. "if they abandon fighting you" [Translator's note: so in the source; the second gloss appears to state the opposite sense]. وَيَكُفُّوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ: i.e. from war. وَأُولئِكُمْ جَعَلْنا لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطاناً مُبِيناً: عليهم stands in the place of the second object.

nahhas-irab:92-92.t: وَما كانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ أَنْ يَقْتُلَ مُؤْمِناً إِلاَّ خَطَأً وَمَنْ قَتَلَ مُؤْمِناً خَطَأً فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ وَدِيَةٌ مُسَلَّمَةٌ إِلى أَهْلِهِ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَصَّدَّقُوا فَإِنْ كانَ مِنْ قَوْمٍ عَدُوٍّ لَكُمْ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ وَإِنْ كانَ مِنْ قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثاقٌ فَدِيَةٌ مُسَلَّمَةٌ إِلى أَهْلِهِ وَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتابِعَيْنِ تَوْبَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً (92) وَما كانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ أَنْ يَقْتُلَ مُؤْمِناً: أَنْ is in the position of the nominative because it is the noun (ism) of كان. إِلَّا خَطَأً: an exception not from the first [category] (a disjoined exception). Sībawayh says «إلا» means "but" (لكن), i.e. "but if he kills him by mistake, then such-and-such is incumbent on him". «إلا» may not mean the wāw ("and"): that is not known in the speech of the Arabs, and it is not sound in meaning, because a mistake is not something that is prohibited. Al-Aʿmash read إلّا خطاءا, with lengthening (madd). وَمَنْ قَتَلَ مُؤْمِناً خَطَأً فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ: i.e. "then the freeing of a slave is incumbent on him". وَدِيَةٌ مُسَلَّمَةٌ إِلى أَهْلِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَصَّدَّقُوا: an exception not from the first [category], i.e. unless the family of the one killed give the blood-money in charity to the killer. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read إلا أن تصّدّقوا with the tāʾ; and according to this reading إلا أن تصدّقوا, with one tāʾ dropped, is allowed; but the light form (without doubling) is not allowed with the yāʾ. In the text (ḥarf) of Ubayy: إلا أن يتصدّقوا. فَإِنْ كانَ مِنْ قَوْمٍ عَدُوٍّ لَكُمْ: such as the Byzantines. فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ: i.e. "then the freeing of a slave is incumbent on the killer". وَإِنْ كانَ مِنْ قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثاقٌ: it was said: by this are meant the protected non-Muslims (ahl al-dhimma); and it was said: by it is meant a Muslim whose lineage is among the ahl al-dhimma. The more appropriate [view] is that the pronoun in كان refers to the believer, because he has been mentioned before. Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ related from Yūnus, from al-Ḥasan, that he read وإن كان من قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق وهو مؤمن ("…while he is a believer"). فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ: nominative by ibtidāʾ (as mubtadaʾ), and the khabar (predicate) is فَصِيامُ شَهْرَيْنِ, i.e. "then fasting two consecutive months is incumbent on him". تَوْبَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ: a maṣdar (verbal noun), or, if you wish, a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); and the nominative is allowed, i.e. "that is a repentance from Allah". إن الله كان عليما: i.e. of what is in the interest of His creation. حَكِيماً: i.e. in the management of the affairs of His servants.

nahhas-irab:93-93.t: وَمَنْ يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِناً مُتَعَمِّداً: a condition (sharṭ), and the answer is فَجَزاؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ. The implied form in Arabic is "Allah will requite him with Hell", and the proof of this is what comes after it [Translator's note: the sentence appears incomplete in the source]. وَغَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: i.e. He punished him. وَلَعَنَهُ: i.e. He removed him far from His mercy and His reward.

nahhas-irab:94-94.t:
إِذا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَتَبَيَّنُوا: it is also read فتثبّتوا ("then verify"). تبيّنوا is stronger in this, because a person may verify and yet not have it become clear. «إذا» has the sense of a condition, and it is sometimes used to govern a requital [in the jussive], as the poet said: [al-Kāmil] 103-
وإذا تصبك خصاصة فتجّمل
(And when poverty befalls you, bear it with dignity.)
The better [usage] is that it not govern a requital, as the poet said: [al-Kāmil] 104-
والنّفس راغبة إذا رغّبتها ... وإذا تردّ إلى قليل تقنع
(The soul is covetous if you make it covet, and when it is brought back to little it is content.)
وَلا تَقُولُوا لِمَنْ أَلْقى إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلامَ لَسْتَ مُؤْمِناً: thus did Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read, and the ḥadīth indicates that, because it is related that Mirdās al-Fadakī passed by Ghālib and said "al-salāmu ʿalaykum", and Ghālib rose to him, killed him and took his property; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed وَلا تَقُولُوا لِمَنْ أَلْقى إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلامَ لَسْتَ مُؤْمِناً. Among the good things that have been said about it is what Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the Muslims passed by a man among his sheep, and he said "Salāmun ʿalaykum", but they killed him and took his sheep; so there was revealed وَلا تَقُولُوا لِمَنْ أَلْقى إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلامَ لَسْتَ مُؤْمِناً — so the ḥadīth has it, with the alif. The people of the two Sanctuaries and the people of Kufa read لمن ألقى إليكم السّلم [i.e. «السَّلَمَ»], and that is allowed, because when he greeted with peace he had offered submission (al-salam). The Arabs say:
ألقى فلان إليّ السّلم, i.e. he yielded and submitted; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said وَأَلْقَوْا إِلَى اللَّهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ السَّلَمَ [al-Naḥl: 87]. Abū Rajāʾ read ولا تقولوا لمن ألقى إليكم السلم with a kasra on the sīn and the lām quiescent [i.e. «السِّلْم»]. Abū Jaʿfar read لَسْتَ مُؤْمِناً [Translator's note: printed identically in the source; Abū Jaʿfar's reading is «مُؤْمَنًا», "granted security"]. فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ مَغانِمُ كَثِيرَةٌ: it is a diptote because it is a plural with no counterpart [pattern] among singulars. كَذلِكَ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative.

nahhas-irab:95-95.t: لا يَسْتَوِي الْقاعِدُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ: this [i.e. «غيرَ», accusative] [Translator's note: the three readings discussed in this entry are all printed «غَيْرُ» in the source; the distinctions are supplied from the explanations] is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries and of Zayd ibn Thābit; غَيْرُ is accusative as the excepted, or, if you wish, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْقاعِدُونَ, i.e. "those who sit are not equal while in their state of health". The ḥadīth indicates the meaning of the accusative: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh and Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiya related from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ, who said: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he said: "Call Zayd for me and tell him to bring the shoulder-blade and the inkpot." Then he said to him: "Write: لا يستوي القاعدون من المؤمنين والمجاهدون في سبيل الله." Ibn Umm Maktūm said: "And I am blind." We had not left before Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ. The people of Kufa and Abū ʿAmr read غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ [i.e. «غيرُ», nominative]; al-Akhfash said: it is an adjective (naʿt) of القاعدين [Translator's note: so in the source, i.e. of القاعدون]. Ḥaywa read غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ [i.e. «غيرِ», genitive], making it an adjective of المؤمنين. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd says it is a badal (substitute), because it is indefinite and the first is definite. فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ الْمُجاهِدِينَ بِأَمْوالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ عَلَى الْقاعِدِينَ دَرَجَةً: and He has said after this:

nahhas-irab:96-96.t: دَرَجاتٍ. The answer is that the meaning of «درجة» is elevation, i.e. He elevated them and raised them by praise, commendation and eulogy — this is the meaning of درجة — while درجات means in Paradise. Ibn Muḥayrīz said: seventy degrees. وَكُلًّا وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنى: accusative by وعد. As for كلّ, it was said: by it the fighters in particular are meant; and it was said: by it are meant the fighters and those with disabilities; and it was said: by it are meant the fighters, those who sit, and those with disabilities, because they are all believers, even though some of them are more excellent than others. وَفَضَّلَ اللَّهُ الْمُجاهِدِينَ عَلَى الْقاعِدِينَ أَجْراً: accusative by فضّل, or, if you wish, it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). «درجات» is a badal (substitute) for أجر; and the nominative is allowed, i.e. "that is degrees".

nahhas-irab:97-97.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ: the noun (ism) of إن, and the khabar (predicate) is فَأُولئِكَ مَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ. تَوَفَّاهُمُ is a past verb, and the masculine came in the sense of "the group" (al-jamīʿ); it may also be an imperfect verb, the original being «تتوفّاهم», with one of the two tāʾs dropped. ظالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the original is ظالمين أنفسهم, then the nūn was dropped and it was put in annexation. قالُوا فِيمَ كُنْتُمْ: the original is «فيما»; the alif was dropped to distinguish between the interrogative and the statement, because a genitive particle precedes it. And the pause, according to the scholars of Arabic, is on it [with hāʾ] [Translator's note: the source reads «والوقوف عند أهل العربية فيه لئلا تحذف الألف والحركة ولأن فيها حرف خفض»; the text appears defective], so that the alif and the vowel are not [both] dropped, and because it contains a genitive particle.

nahhas-irab:98-98.t: إِلَّا الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ: accusative as the excepted, i.e. except those who are truly oppressed. لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً: in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "not able"; and likewise وَلا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلًا.

nahhas-irab:100-100.t:
وَمَنْ يُهاجِرْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يَجِدْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُراغَماً: a condition (sharṭ) and its answer. Mujāhid said: al-murgham [Translator's note: so in the source, for «المراغم»] is:
the place one moves away to. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: al-murāgham is the place one moves to. Al-Kisāʾī said: al-murāgham is:
the way to go. Abū ʿUbayda said: al-murāgham is the place of emigration. Abū Jaʿfar said: these views agree in meaning: al-murāgham is the way to go and the place one moves to in a state of emigration; it is a noun for the place in which one defies [others] (yurāghim), and it is derived from al-rughām (dust). رغم أنف فلان means "so-and-so's nose stuck to the dust"; راغمت فلانا means "I abandoned him and showed him hostility, and did not care if his nose was rubbed in the dust"; رغم الله أمره [Translator's note: so in the source]. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: وَسَعَةً, in provision. وَمَنْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ مُهاجِراً إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ: a condition (sharṭ). ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ الْمَوْتُ: conjoined (maʿṭūf); it may not be the answer, because «ثم» puts what comes second with it at a distance from the first, whereas with the fāʾ the second is close to the first. The answer is فَقَدْ وَقَعَ أَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ.

nahhas-irab:101-101.t:
«أن» [Translator's note: i.e. أَنْ تَقْصُرُوا مِنَ الصَّلاةِ] is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "in shortening" (في أن تقصروا). Abū ʿUbayda said: there are three forms of it; one says:
قصرت الصلاة, قصّرتها and أقصرتها. إِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَنْ يَفْتِنَكُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: al-Farrāʾ said: the people of the Ḥijāz say فتنت الرجل, while Tamīm, Rabīʿa, Qays, Asad and all the people of Najd say أفتنت الرجل. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh distinguished between them, saying: فتنته means "I put fitna (trial, enticement) into him", like عجلته, and أفتنته means "I made him infatuated". Al-Aṣmaʿī claimed that he did not know أفتنته with the alif.

nahhas-irab:102-102.t: وَإِذا كُنْتَ فِيهِمْ فَأَقَمْتَ لَهُمُ الصَّلاةَ فَلْتَقُمْ: the original is فلتقم [i.e. «فَلِتَقُمْ», with kasra on the lām]; the kasra was dropped because of its heaviness. Al-Akhfash, al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ reported that the lām of command, the lām of kay (purpose) and the lām of denial (juḥūd) are [sometimes] given a fatḥa; Sībawayh disallows this for a compelling reason, namely the distinction between the lām of the genitive and the lām of emphasis. Abū Isḥāq said: no attention is paid to the report of a reporter which the early grammarians did not transmit; and even if the one who reports it is truthful, the one from whom he heard it is mistaken. And likewise وَلْيَأْخُذُوا أَسْلِحَتَهُمْ, and likewise فَلْيَكُونُوا مِنْ وَرائِكُمْ وَلْتَأْتِ طائِفَةٌ أُخْرى لَمْ يُصَلُّوا فَلْيُصَلُّوا مَعَكَ. وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنْ كانَ بِكُمْ أَذىً: [أذى] is in the position of the nominative, except that it ends in a short alif (maqṣūr). «أن تضعوا» is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "in laying down" (في أن تضعوا).

nahhas-irab:103-103.t: فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ قِياماً وَقُعُوداً وَعَلى جُنُوبِكُمْ: a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:104-104.t: وَلا تَهِنُوا فِي ابْتِغاءِ الْقَوْمِ: a prohibition. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj read إِنْ تَكُونُوا تَأْلَمُونَ with a fatḥa on the hamza [i.e. «أَنْ تكونوا»], meaning "because" (لأن). Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir read إن تكونوا تيلمون with a kasra on the tāʾ, to indicate that it is from [the pattern] faʿila. According to the Basrans, a kasra on the tāʾ in تألمون is not allowed, because of the heaviness of the kasra in it.

nahhas-irab:105-105.t: إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ بِالْحَقِّ لِتَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ: the lām of kay (purpose). It is related of al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAmr that they assimilated the mīm into the bāʾ; the grammarians do not allow that, because the mīm has nasalisation (ghunna).

nahhas-irab:112-112.t:
وَمَنْ يَكْسِبْ خَطِيئَةً أَوْ إِثْماً:
a condition (sharṭ). ثُمَّ يَرْمِ بِهِ:
conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; and in the speech there is an omission from the first [part], according to the school of Sībawayh. It is asked: what is the difference between al-khaṭīʾa and al-ithm, when one of them has been conjoined to the other? There are several answers to this: one of them is that they are one [thing], but since the two words differ, this is allowed. It was also said: al-khaṭīʾa may be minor, while al-ithm can only be major. Abū Isḥāq said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, named some acts of disobedience khaṭāyā and named some ithm; so He informed [us] that whoever commits an act of disobedience that is called khaṭīʾa, or commits an act of disobedience that is called ithm, and then accuses of it someone who did not do it and is innocent of it, فَقَدِ احْتَمَلَ بُهْتاناً وَإِثْماً مُبِيناً.
Al-buhtān is the lie at whose enormity and gravity one is bewildered.

nahhas-irab:113-113.t:
وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَتُهُ:
what follows «لولا» is nominative by ibtidāʾ (as mubtadaʾ) according to Sībawayh, and the khabar (predicate) is omitted and is not made overt. The meaning is: "were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, in that He alerted you to the truth", لَهَمَّتْ طائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يُضِلُّوكَ
from the truth; because they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to clear Ibn Ubayriq of the accusation and to attach it to the Jew. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, favoured His Messenger ﷺ by alerting him to that and informing him of it. وَما يُضِلُّونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ:
because they do the deed of those who go astray, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, protects His Messenger ﷺ. وَما يَضُرُّونَكَ مِنْ شَيْءٍ:
because you are protected. وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَعَلَّمَكَ ما لَمْ تَكُنْ تَعْلَمُ:
the ḍamma was dropped from the nūn for the jussive, and the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. «تعلم» is in the position of the accusative because it is the khabar (predicate) of «تكن».

nahhas-irab:114-114.t:
لا خَيْرَ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِنْ نَجْواهُمْ إِلَّا مَنْ أَمَرَ بِصَدَقَةٍ: نجواهم has two meanings in Arabic:
one of them is that it is what they confer secretly about and summon one another to. If it is in this sense, «فمن» is in the position of the accusative, because it is an exception not from the first [category], i.e. "but whoever enjoins charity, or what is right, or reconciliation between people, and calls to it — in his secret conference there is good". «من» may also be in the position of the genitive, the implied form being "except in the secret conference of whoever enjoins charity". The other meaning is that al-najwā is the group of those who have withdrawn apart; so (من) here is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute), and in the position of the accusative according to the view of those who say ما مررت بأحد إلّا زيدا. Najwā is derived from نجوت الشيء أنجوه, i.e. "I extracted it and set it apart"; and al-najwa of land is the elevated part, because it stands apart by its elevation from what is around it, as the poet said: [al-Basīṭ] 105-
فمن بنجوته كمن بعقوته ... والمستكنّ كمن يمشي بقرواح
(The one on his high ground is like the one in his courtyard, and the one sheltered is like one who walks on bare open land.)
وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ: a condition (sharṭ). ابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاتِ اللَّهِ: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). And the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أَجْراً عَظِيماً: the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness, and it may be brought according to the original form in poetry.

nahhas-irab:115-115.t: وَمَنْ يُشاقِقِ الرَّسُولَ: jussive because it is a condition. The doubling appears [unassimilated] because the second qāf is in a position of quiescence, and it takes a kasra only so that two quiescent letters do not meet. His saying نُوَلِّهِ ما تَوَلَّى: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). If you wish, you drop the yāʾ and leave the kasra to indicate it; if you wish, you give [the hāʾ] a ḍamma and keep the wāw; and if you wish, you drop it. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned its reasons. As for making the hāʾ quiescent, it is not allowed, because of its faintness; and likewise وَنُصْلِهِ جَهَنَّمَ. وَساءَتْ مَصِيراً: accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz, specification).

nahhas-irab:117-117.t:
إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا إِناثاً: a mafʿūl (object); and likewise وَإِنْ يَدْعُونَ إِلَّا شَيْطاناً مَرِيداً. Abū Rajāʾ said, from al-Ḥasan: in every tribe there was an idol called "the female of the Banū So-and-so", so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا إِناثاً وَإِنْ. Ibn ʿAbbās said: with every idol there was a she-devil. And it was said:
إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا إِناثاً because stones are feminine, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, mentioned them with lowliness, because the masculine of everything is higher than the feminine; وَإِنْ يَدْعُونَ إِلَّا شَيْطاناً مَرِيداً because he commanded them to do that, so the invoking was attributed to him figuratively, because they obey him in it.

nahhas-irab:118-118.t: لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ: [part] of its adjective (naʿt); and it may be an imprecation against him. وَقالَ لَأَتَّخِذَنَّ مِنْ عِبادِكَ نَصِيباً مَفْرُوضاً: it was said: [part] of the share is their obeying him in things, among them that they drive a nail for the newborn at its birth and carry it around on its seventh day, saying: "So that the jinn-dwellers (al-ʿummār) may know him."

nahhas-irab:119-119.t: وَلَأُضِلَّنَّهُمْ: i.e. from the truth. وَلَأُمَنِّيَنَّهُمْ: i.e. [hopes of] long life, good, repentance and forgiveness while persisting [in sin]. وَلَآمُرَنَّهُمْ فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلْقَ اللَّهِ: these are lāms of the oath, and the nūn is required with them, because one swears only about the future. The people of tafsīr — Mujāhid and others — say that the meaning of فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلْقَ اللَّهِ is the religion of Allah. It has been said: castration is meant by it, and the marks that the Zanj and the Abyssinians make [on their bodies]. And it was said: it is that Allah created the sun, the moon and stones for benefit, but they turned that around and worshipped them apart from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. وَمَنْ يَتَّخِذِ الشَّيْطانَ وَلِيًّا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ: [i.e.] obeys him and leaves the command of Allah.

nahhas-irab:120-120.t: يَعِدُهُمْ: i.e. he promises them leadership, standing and wealth so that they disobey Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. وَما يَعِدُهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ إِلَّا غُرُوراً: i.e. deception.

nahhas-irab:121-121.t: فأُولئِكَ: a mubtadaʾ (subject). مَأْواهُمْ: a second mubtadaʾ. جَهَنَّمُ: the khabar (predicate) of the second, and the clause is the khabar of the first. وَلا يَجِدُونَ عَنْها مَحِيصاً: i.e. a refuge; the verb from it is حاص يحيص.

nahhas-irab:122-122.t:
وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ: nominative by ibtidāʾ (as mubtadaʾ), and the khabar (predicate) is سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ. Or, if you wish, it is in the position of the accusative by an implied verb explained by what follows it, and that is good because it is conjoined.
وَمَنْ أَصْدَقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ: mubtadaʾ and khabar. قِيلًا: as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz, specification). One says قيلا, قولا and قالا.

nahhas-irab:123-123.t: لَيْسَ بِأَمانِيِّكُمْ وَلا أَمانِيِّ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ: Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read لَيْسَ بِأَمانِيِّكُمْ وَلا أَمانِيِّ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ with the yāʾ light in both [Translator's note: the source prints the doubled yāʾ in the quotation]. Among the best of what has been related about it is what al-Ḥakam ibn Abān related from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the Jews and the Christians said: "None will enter Paradise except those who are of us"; and Quraysh said: "We will not be resurrected." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed لَيْسَ بِأَمانِيِّكُمْ وَلا أَمانِيِّ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ. مَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءاً يُجْزَ بِهِ: he said: al-sūʾ here is associating partners [with Allah]. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: al-sūʾ is disbelief, and what one is requited for of what one has not repented of.

nahhas-irab:124-124.t:
وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحاتِ: jussive by the condition, and the requital is فَأُولئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ.
وَلا يُظْلَمُونَ نَقِيراً: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.

nahhas-irab:125-125.t:
وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). وَلَهَدَيْناهُمْ [Translator's note: so in the source; this phrase belongs to 4:68. The word meant here is evidently «دِيناً» of this verse]: as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz, specification). وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ: mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَاتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ إِبْراهِيمَ خَلِيلًا: we have mentioned its meaning. Among the best of what has been said about it is that al-khalīl is the one singled out: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, singled him out in his time for the message. The proof of this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «وقد اتّخذ الله عزّ وجلّ صاحبكم خليلا» ("Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has taken your companion as a khalīl"), meaning himself ﷺ; and he ﷺ said: «لو كنت متّخذا خليلا لاتّخذت أبا بكر خليلا» ("Were I to take a khalīl, I would take Abū Bakr as a khalīl"), i.e. were I to single out anyone for something, I would single out Abū Bakr.
In this there is a refutation of whoever claimed that the Prophet ﷺ singled out some of his Companions for something of the matter of religion.

nahhas-irab:127-127.t: وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ فِي النِّساءِ قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ وَما يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتابِ فِي يَتامَى النِّساءِ اللاَّتِي لا تُؤْتُونَهُنَّ ما كُتِبَ لَهُنَّ وَتَرْغَبُونَ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الْوِلْدانِ وَأَنْ تَقُومُوا لِلْيَتامى بِالْقِسْطِ وَما تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِهِ عَلِيماً (127) ما is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "and the Qur'an gives you a ruling". وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الْوِلْدانِ: in the position of the genitive, because it is conjoined to اليتامى; and likewise وَأَنْ تَقُومُوا لِلْيَتامى بِالْقِسْطِ.

nahhas-irab:128-128.t:
وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِها نُشُوزاً أَوْ إِعْراضاً: you make امرأة nominative by an implied verb which what follows it explains. This is good only with إن, because of its strength in the domain of conditional requital, and when the verb is past; it is allowed with the imperfect in poetry, and Sībawayh recited: [al-Khafīf] 106-
وإذا واغل ينبهم يحيّوه ... وتعطف عليه كأس السّاقي
(And when an uninvited guest comes upon them, they greet him, and the cupbearer's cup is turned towards him.)
The view of whoever said that خفت means "I was certain" is mistaken. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "and if a woman fears from her husband the continuation of recalcitrance". Abū Jaʿfar said: the difference between al-nushūz and al-iʿrāḍ is that al-nushūz is keeping distant, and al-iʿrāḍ is that he does not speak to her or find comfort with her. فلا جناح عليهما أن يصّالحا بينهما صلحا: this is the reading of the Medinans; the Kufans read أَنْ يُصْلِحا; and ʿĀṣim (al-Jaḥdarī) read أن يصلحا with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, the ṣād doubled and with a fatḥa [i.e. «يَصَّلَحا»]. They all read صلحا, except that it is related of al-Aʿmash that he read إلّا أن يصلحا بينهما إصلاحا. Abū Jaʿfar said: all this is construed according to the meaning, as one says هو يدعه تركا ("he leaves it, an abandoning"). Whoever said يصلحا, the maṣdar is إصلاحا on his view, and صلح is a noun; whoever said يصّالحا, the maṣdar is إصلاحا [Translator's note: so in the source; «تصالُحًا» would be expected], the original being تصالحا, then it was assimilated; and whoever said يصّلحا, the original for him is يصطلحا اصطلاحا, then it is assimilated. Similar to it is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays: [al-Ṭawīl] 107-
ورضت فذلّت صعبة أيّ إذلال
(I broke in a stubborn one, and she was humbled — what a humbling!)
And al-Quṭāmī said: [al-Wāfir] 108-
وخير الأمر ما استقبلت منه ... وليس بأن تتبّعه اتّباعا
(The best of an affair is what you meet at its beginning, not by following it up behind.)
because the meaning of تتبّعه and تتّبعه is one. The grammarians have two views about this. Some of them say:
what governs it is an omitted verb, and the meaning is "except that they make peace between them, and the matter is set right with a settlement"; on this view, the maṣdar is not referred to by an attached pronoun. Others say: what governs it is the first [verb], and the speech is construed according to the meaning; on this [view] it is referred to by an attached pronoun. This is set out in explanation in the chapter on the definite article.
وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). وَأُحْضِرَتِ الْأَنْفُسُ الشُّحَّ: i.e. it is stingy with what benefit it has in it.
وَإِنْ تُحْسِنُوا وَتَتَّقُوا: i.e. if you prefer doing good and piety and so make companionship beautiful. فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيراً: and since He is aware of it, He will requite it.

nahhas-irab:129-129.t: وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا بَيْنَ النِّساءِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ: it was said: in allotment [of nights], gentleness and clothing; al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: in love and intercourse. فَلا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ: a maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: and do not incline to the young one and leave the other neither unmarried, so that she may marry, nor with a husband. فَتَذَرُوها: accusative because it is the answer to the prohibition. كَالْمُعَلَّقَةِ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative.

nahhas-irab:131-131.t: وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الذين». أَنِ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ: in the position of the accusative. Al-Akhfash said: i.e. "that you fear Allah" (بأن تتقوا الله).

nahhas-irab:133-133.t: إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ: a condition (sharṭ) and its answer. وَيَأْتِ بِآخَرِينَ: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the answer.

nahhas-irab:134-134.t: مَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ: [يريد is] in the position of the accusative because it is the khabar (predicate) of كان. فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ ثَوابُ الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ: nominative by ibtidāʾ (as mubtadaʾ).

nahhas-irab:135-135.t: كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَداءَ: an adjective (naʿt) of قوّامين; or, if you wish, it is a khabar after a khabar. Better than these two is that it be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the reference to «الذين آمنوا» contained in قوامين, because the meaning then becomes "be upholders of justice when you bear witness and at the time of your witnessing". It is a diptote because it contains the alif of the feminine. وَلَوْ عَلى أَنْفُسِكُمْ: i.e. even if the right is against yourselves. أَوِ الْوالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ: conjoined with أو. إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا: the khabar (predicate) of يكن, whose noun is latent in it, i.e. "if the one claimed against is rich". أَوْ فَقِيراً فَاللَّهُ أَوْلى بِهِما: He did not say به, whereas «أو» indicates only that it holds for one of the two. The grammarians have several answers about this. Al-Akhfash said: «أو» may mean the wāw ("and"). He said: it may also be that the implied form is "if those who dispute (من تخاصم) are two rich or two poor", and He said غنيا construing it according to the wording of من, like وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ [Muḥammad: 16], whose meaning is "they listen". Abū Jaʿfar said: both views are mistaken: «أو» does not mean the wāw, and من is not implied, just as part of a noun is not implied. And it was said: He said بهما only because both had been mentioned before, as He said وَلَهُ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ فَلِكُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ [al-Nisāʾ: 12]. أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا: in the position of the accusative. Ibn ʿĀmir and the Kufans read وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا [Translator's note: so printed in the source; the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamza is «تَلُوا», as the end of this entry shows], and we have mentioned it. Its verb is لوى; its original is لوي, the yāʾ having been changed to alif because of its vowel and the vowel of what precedes it. The maṣdar is ليّا, the original being لويا, and ليّانا, the original being لويانا; then the wāw was assimilated. In the ḥadīth: «ليّ الواجد يحلّ عقوبته وعرضه» ("The procrastination of one who is able [to pay] makes lawful his punishment and his honour"). Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: his punishment is his imprisonment, and his honour is complaining about him. One of the grammarians claimed that whoever read (تلوا) [has it] in the sense of «تلووا», the original being تلؤوا: the wāw was given a hamza, as one says أُقِّتَتْ, so it became تلؤوا; then the hamza was lightened and its vowel was cast onto the lām, so it had to be dropped, and it became تلو [Translator's note: so in the source, i.e. «تَلُوا»].

nahhas-irab:137-137.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا: the noun (ism) of «إنّ», and the khabar (predicate) is لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ. It is asked: Allah does not forgive any [degree] of disbelief, so how did He say إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدادُوا كُفْراً لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ? The answer is that when the disbeliever believes, his disbelief is forgiven him; then if he goes back and disbelieves, the first disbelief is not forgiven him. The meaning of «ثم ازدادوا كفرا» is "they persisted in disbelief". لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا: i.e. a path to Paradise; and it was said: He does not single them out for divine enablement (tawfīq) as He singles out His friends.

nahhas-irab:138-139.t: بَشِّرِ الْمُنافِقِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكافِرِينَ أَوْلِياءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: an adjective (naʿt) of المنافقين. In this there is proof that whoever among the monotheists commits an act of disobedience is not a hypocrite, because he does not take the disbelievers as allies. أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ: i.e. do they seek to gain might through them? فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعاً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:140-140.t: By this He indicated the obligation of avoiding the people of disobedience when something reprehensible appears from them, because whoever does not avoid them has approved their deed, and approval of disbelief is disbelief. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said إِنَّكُمْ إِذاً مِثْلُهُمْ. إِنَّ اللَّهَ جامِعُ الْمُنافِقِينَ: the original has tanwīn [i.e. «جامعٌ المنافقين»], and it was dropped for lightness.

nahhas-irab:141-141.t: الَّذِينَ يَتَرَبَّصُونَ بِكُمْ: an adjective (naʿt) of المنافقين. فَإِنْ كانَ لَكُمْ فَتْحٌ: the noun of كان; and likewise وَإِنْ كانَ لِلْكافِرِينَ نَصِيبٌ. قالُوا أَلَمْ نَسْتَحْوِذْ عَلَيْكُمْ: it came according to the original form; had it been made weak (iʿlāl), it would have been لم نستحذ. The verb with the weakening is استحاذ يستحيذ, and without the weakening استحوذ يستحوذ. In the text (ḥarf) of Ubayy: ومنعناكم من المؤمنين; it is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is "we have gained mastery over you"; and it may be on the basis of the omission of قد. We have mentioned the meaning of وَلَنْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لِلْكافِرِينَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ سَبِيلًا.

nahhas-irab:142-142.t:
إِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ يُخادِعُونَ اللَّهَ:
figurative (majāz), i.e. they deceive the friends of Allah. وَهُوَ خادِعُهُمْ:
i.e. He punishes them. If you wish, you make the hāʾ quiescent and say «وهْو», because the ḍamma is heavy and a wāw precedes the word; making the wāw quiescent has also been reported. Maslama ibn ʿAbd Allāh the grammarian read وَهُوَ خادِعُهُمْ
with the ʿayn quiescent; Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: this is a solecism (laḥn), because it is the loss of the case-ending. Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh allowed that, and recited: [al-Rajaz] 109-
إذا اعوججن قلت صاحب قوّم
(When they [the camels] went crooked, I said: "Companion, straighten [them]!")
وَإِذا قامُوا إِلَى الصَّلاةِ قامُوا كُسالى:
in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and likewise يراءون الناس, i.e. they show people that they are devout through their prayer. Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Aʿraj read يرؤّون الناس on the pattern of يُدَعُّونَ [al-Ṭūr: 13], and it was reported that it is the dialect of lower Muḍar. The first reading is preferable, because of their consensus on الذين هم يراءون. One says فلان مراء ("so-and-so is a hypocrite") and فعل ذلك رئاء الناس ("he did that to be seen by people"). وَلا يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا:
i.e. they do not remember Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, by recitation or glorification; they remember Him only by the takbīr and by what they show off with. The implied form is "except a little remembrance".

nahhas-irab:143-143.t: مُذَبْذَبِينَ بَيْنَ ذلِكَ: i.e. wavering: they show these that they are of them, and those that they are of them. In the text (ḥarf) of Ubayy: متذبذبين; and assimilation is allowed according to this reading: مُذَبْذَبِينَ [Translator's note: printed with the standard vowelling in the source; the form described is «مُذَّبْذِبِينَ»], with the first dhāl doubled and the second with kasra. It is related from al-Ḥasan [that he read] مذبذبين with a fatḥa on the mīm.

nahhas-irab:144-144.t: لا تَتَّخِذُوا الْكافِرِينَ أَوْلِياءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: two objects (mafʿūlān), i.e. do not make them your intimates and confidants. أَتُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ سُلْطاناً مُبِيناً: i.e. [an argument] for His punishing you.

nahhas-irab:145-145.t:
إِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ فِي الدَّرْكِ الْأَسْفَلِ مِنَ النَّارِ: the Kufans read فِي الدَّرْكِ [Translator's note: the two readings are printed identically in the source; the Kufan reading is «الدَّرْكِ» with the rāʾ quiescent, the other «الدَّرَكِ» with fatḥa], and the first is more eloquent; the proof of that is that its plural is said to be أدراك, like جمل and أجمال. We have mentioned that al-adrāk are the layers and stations, except that the usage of the Arabs is to call everything that descends:
أدراك — one says of a well: أدراك — and to call what ascends درج; so Paradise has darajāt (degrees) and the Fire has adrāk (depths).

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ): «يا» is a particle with which one calls, and it may be omitted when the one addressed is aware of being called. «أيّ» is a single-word vocative (munādā mufrad), and «ها» is for drawing attention (tanbīh). «النّاس» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أيّ»; its accusative according to the position [of «أيّ»] is not permissible, because the speech is not complete before it — except according to the view of al-Māzinī. Al-Akhfash claimed that «أيّ» is a relative completed by the adjective, but a ṣila (relative clause) is only known to be a clause. (اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ): an imperative, and for that reason the nūn has been dropped from it. (الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ) is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective). (مِنْ نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ): made feminine according to the wording; in ordinary speech «من نفس واحد» is also permissible, and likewise (وَخَلَقَ مِنْها زَوْجَها). (وَبَثَّ مِنْهُما): the masculine and the feminine in the dual have one and the same form of marker, whereas the plural is not so, because it differs while the dual agrees. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسائَلُونَ بِهِ): this is the reading of the people of Medina, with assimilation of the tāʾ into the sīn [«تسّاءلون»]; and the reading of the people of Kufa is تَسائَلُونَ, dropping a tāʾ because two tāʾs come together and because the meaning is known; and like it is إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ بِأَلْسِنَتِكُمْ [al-Nūr: 15]. (وَالْأَرْحامَ): conjoined, i.e. and fear [Allah regarding] the ties of kinship, lest you sever them. Ibrāhīm, Qatāda and Ḥamza read وَالْأَرْحامَ in the genitive [«والأرحامِ»], and the grammarians have spoken about that. As for the Basrans, their leaders said: it is a solecism (laḥn) with which reciting is not lawful. As for the Kufans, they said: it is ugly, and they did not add to this nor mention the reason for its ugliness, as far as I know. Sībawayh said: one does not conjoin to the genitive pronoun, because it is like the tanwīn. Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī said: the conjoined and what it is conjoined to are partners; nothing enters one of them except what enters the other; so just as «مررت بزيد وك» (I passed by Zayd and -you) is not permissible, likewise «مررت بك وزيد» (I passed by you and Zayd) is not permissible. It has occurred in poetry, as the poet said: [al-Basīṭ] 91-
فاليوم قرّبت تهجونا وتشتمنا ... فاذهب فما بك والأيّام من عجب
(Today you have come close, satirising and reviling us; so go — there is nothing wondrous in you and in the times.)
And as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 92-
وما بينها والكعب غوط نفانف
(And between it and the ankle-bone are deep, wide hollows.)
Some of them said: (وَالْأَرْحامَ) [in the genitive] is an oath; this is wrong in meaning and in iʿrāb, because the ḥadīth from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ indicates the accusative. Shuʿba related from ʿAwn ibn Abī Juḥayfa, from al-Nadhr ibn Jarīr [Translator's note: so printed; the narrator is known as al-Mundhir ibn Jarīr], from his father, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ when a group from Muḍar [Translator's note: printed «مصر» (Egypt); the known version of the ḥadīth has «مضر» (Muḍar)] came, barefoot and naked, and I saw the face of the Prophet ﷺ change at what he saw of their need. Then he prayed the noon prayer and addressed the people, and said: «O people, fear your Lord, and the ties of kinship»; then he said: «Let a man give in charity from his dinar, let a man give in charity from his dirham, let a man give in charity from his ṣāʿ of dates», and he mentioned the ḥadīth. So the meaning of this is according to the accusative, because he urged them to maintain the ties of their kinship. Also, if it were an oath, something would have been omitted from it, because the meaning would be «and they say: by the ties of kinship», i.e. «by the Lord of the ties of kinship»; and omission is permissible only when the speech is not sound except with it. Also, it is soundly established from the Prophet ﷺ: «Whoever swears, let him swear by Allah»; so just as it is not permissible for you to swear except by Allah, likewise it is not permissible for you to ask someone to swear except by Allah; and this refutes the view of whoever says that the meaning is «I ask you by Allah and by the tie of kinship». Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning of (تَسائَلُونَ بِهِ) is: you demand your rights by Him; and on this basis the genitive has no meaning. «الرحم» is feminine, and one says «رَحِم», «رِحْم», «رَحْم» and «رُحْم» [Translator's note: the four forms are printed identically, without vowels; the usual list is given here]. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيباً): Ibn ʿAbbās said: i.e. watchful (ḥafīẓ). Abū Jaʿfar said: one says «رقب الرجل» and «قد رقبته رقبة ورقبانا» (I watched him).

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: (وَآتُوا الْيَتامى أَمْوالَهُمْ): two objects. One does not say «يتيم» (orphan) except of one who has reached less than ten [years]; and it has been said: one does not say «يتيم» except of one who has not reached puberty. It is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: «There is no orphanhood after puberty». (وَلا تَتَبَدَّلُوا الْخَبِيثَ بِالطَّيِّبِ), i.e. do not consume the property of orphans, which is forbidden and bad, and leave the good, which is your own property. (ولا تأكلوا أموالهم إلى أموالكم), i.e. do not combine them and consume them both. (إِنَّهُ كانَ حُوباً كَبِيراً): al-Ḥasan read حُوباً [Translator's note: presumably «حَوْبا», with fatḥa]. Al-Akhfash said: it is the dialect of the Banū Tamīm; «الحَوب» is the maṣdar (verbal noun), as is «الحيابة», and «الحُوب» is the noun. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «ولا تّبدّلوا», assimilating the tāʾ into the tāʾ and combining two quiescent letters; that is permissible because the first quiescent letter is a letter of prolongation and softness; but this is not permissible in His saying ناراً تَلَظَّى [al-Layl: 14].

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
(وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تُقْسِطُوا فِي الْيَتامى): a condition, i.e. if you fear that you will not act justly regarding their dowries [and] in spending on them. (فَانْكِحُوا ما طابَ لَكُمْ مِنَ النِّساءِ): by this He indicated that «نساء» (women) is said only of those who have reached puberty.
The singular of «النساء» is «نسوة», and «نسوة» has no singular from its own root; instead one says «امرأة». It may be asked: how did «ما» come to be used for human beings? There are two answers to this. Al-Farrāʾ said: «ما» here is maṣdariyya; this is very far-fetched — «فانكحوا الطيبة» (so marry the goodness) is not sound. The Basrans said: «ما» is used for attributes, just as «ما» is used for what does not have reason; one says «ما عندك؟» (what is with you?), and the answer is «ظريف وكريم» (a witty one and a noble one). So the meaning is: marry the good among women, i.e. the lawful; and what Allah has forbidden is not good. (مَثْنى وَثُلاثَ وَرُباعَ) is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from «ما». According to most of the Basrans it is a diptote both when definite and indefinite, because it has two causes, one of them being that it is deflected (maʿdūl). Abū Isḥāq said:
and the other is that it is deflected from a feminine. Someone else said: the cause is that it is deflected, conveying repetition — it is sound that it is not written [Translator's note: this phrase («صحّ أنها لا تكتب») is obscure in the source and is translated literally] — and this is preferable, [since] Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: أُولِي أَجْنِحَةٍ مَثْنى وَثُلاثَ وَرُباعَ [Fāṭir: 1], and this is deflected from a masculine. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is a diptote because there is in it the sense of annexation and of the alif and lām. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted it to be declined fully (triptote) in counting, on the basis that it is indefinite. Al-Akhfash claimed that if something is named with it, it is declined fully both when definite and indefinite, because deflection has left it. (فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ) is in the position of the jussive by the condition. (أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا) is in the position of the accusative by «خفتم». (فَواحِدَةً), i.e. «فانكحوا واحدة» (then marry one). Al-Aʿraj read فَواحِدَةً in the nominative [«فواحدةٌ»]; al-Kisāʾī said: the implied construction is «فواحدة تقنع» (then one suffices). (أَوْ ما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ) is conjoined to «واحدة». (ذلِكَ أَدْنى): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). (أَلَّا تَعُولُوا) is in the position of the accusative.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
(وَآتُوا النِّساءَ صَدُقاتِهِنَّ): two objects; the singular is «صَدُقة». Al-Akhfash said: the Banū Tamīm say «صُدْقة», and the plural is «صُدُقات»; if you wish you may give [the dāl] a fatḥa, and if you wish a sukūn. Al-Māzinī said: one says «صِداق المرأة» (the woman's dower) with kasra, and it is not said with fatḥa; but Yaʿqūb [ibn al-Sikkīt] and Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] related the fatḥa. (فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْساً): an address to the husbands. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that it is an address to the guardians, because they used to take the dowry and not give the woman any of it, so nothing of it was permitted to them except what the woman gave up willingly. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first view is preferable, because there has been no mention of the guardians.
(نَفْساً) is accusative as clarification (al-bayān, i.e. tamyīz). Neither Sībawayh nor the Kufans permit what is for clarification to be fronted; al-Māzinī and Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] permitted it to be fronted when the governing factor is a verb, and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 93-
وما كان نفيسا بالفراق تطيب
(And the soul was not content with the parting.) [Translator's note: «نفيسا» is so printed; the verse is usually cited as «نفسا»; see the following remark.]
And I heard Abū Isḥāq say: the [correct] transmission is only «وما كان نفسي» (and my soul was not). (فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئاً مَرِيئاً): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ. One says «هنؤ الطعام ومرؤ» (the food was wholesome and agreeable), so it is «هنيء مريء» on the pattern faʿīl; and «هنئ يهنأ» so it is «هنئ» on the pattern faʿil, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is on the pattern faʿal; and «قد هنأني ومرأني» (it was wholesome and agreeable to me); but if you use it alone you say «أمرأني» with an alif.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
(وَلا تُؤْتُوا السُّفَهاءَ أَمْوالَكُمُ): Sālim al-Afṭas related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, concerning (وَلا تُؤْتُوا السُّفَهاءَ أَمْوالَكُمُ), that he said: he means the orphans: do not give them their property — as He said: وَلا تَقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ [al-Nisāʾ: 29]. This is among the best things said about the verse, and its explanation in Arabic is: do not give the foolish the property which you own and they own, as He said: وَنِساءِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ [al-Aḥzāb: 59]. Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid related from Abū Mālik, concerning (وَلا تُؤْتُوا السُّفَهاءَ أَمْوالَكُمُ), that he said:
your children: do not give them your property, lest they ruin it and be left with nothing. Sufyān related from Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj, from Mujāhid, concerning (وَلا تُؤْتُوا السُّفَهاءَ أَمْوالَكُمُ), that he said: women. Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is not sound; the Arabs say of women only «سفائه». It has also been said: «ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم» is an address to the guardians (al-awṣiyāʾ); the property is annexed to them, even though it is not theirs, by extension of usage, because it is in their hands, as one says «بسر النخلة» (the unripe dates of the palm) and «ماء البئر» (the water of the well). And it has been said: «ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم» is literal, i.e. do not give them the property that you own; this is far-fetched, because after it comes (وَارْزُقُوهُمْ فِيها وَاكْسُوهُمْ وَقُولُوا لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفاً): a maṣdar (verbal noun) and its naʿt (adjective). Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī read «ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم اللاتي جعل الله لكم», as the plural of «التي», while the reading of the generality is (الَّتِي), according to the form of the group [i.e. the feminine singular for a non-human plural]. Al-Farrāʾ said: the more frequent [usage] in the speech of the Arabs is «النساء اللواتي» and «الأموال التي», and likewise for things other than property. The people of Kufa read (قِياماً), the people of Medina read «قيما», and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar read «قواما». Al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī claimed that «قياما» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. «and do not give the foolish your property by which your affairs are set right, so that you stand by them, a standing». Al-Akhfash said: the meaning is «maintaining your affairs» — he takes it to be a plural. «قيّما» and «قواما» according to al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ have the meaning of «قياما». The Basrans said: «قيم» is the plural of «قيمة», i.e. Allah made it the value of things.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: (وَابْتَلُوا الْيَتامى حَتَّى إِذا): Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read «رَشَدا» [in «فإن آنستم منهم رشدا»], which is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «رشِد», and «رُشْد» is the maṣdar of «رشَد», and likewise «الرّشاد». (وَلا تَأْكُلُوها إِسْرافاً): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and it may also be a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَبِداراً) is conjoined to it. (أَنْ يَكْبَرُوا) is in the position of the accusative by «بدار». (وَمَنْ كانَ غَنِيًّا فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ): a condition and its apodosis, and likewise (وَمَنْ كانَ فَقِيراً فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ). (فَإِذا دَفَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوالَهُمْ فَأَشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِمْ): «إذا» is used as a conditional [with the jussive] in poetry, because it needs an apodosis, and only a verb follows it, overt or implied; but it is not used as a conditional outside poetry according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, because what follows it differs from what follows the conditional particles, since it is something certain. Al-Khalīl said: you say «آتيك إذا احمرّ البسر» (I will come to you when the dates turn red), and you do not say «إن احمرّ البسر» (if the dates turn red).

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
(لِلرِّجالِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوالِدانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ): in the position of the nominative, as a mubtadaʾ (subject) or by the adverbial phrase (al-ṣifa).
(مِمَّا قَلَّ مِنْهُ أَوْ كَثُرَ نَصِيباً مَفْرُوضاً): Abū Isḥāq said: (نَصِيباً مَفْرُوضاً) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), as you say «فرضا» (as an obligation); had it not been a maṣdar, it would have been nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «نصيب».

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: It is unlikely that this is by way of recommendation (al-nadb), because recommendation is established only by evidence, consensus or a prophetic stipulation (tawqīf). The best thing said about it is that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, commanded that when relatives who do not inherit are present, the one who does inherit should give to them, out of thanks to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, for having favoured him.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
(وَلْيَخْشَ): jussive by the command, and for that reason the alif has been dropped from it. Sībawayh said: [the lām is required] lest the jussive resemble the nominative and the accusative. The Kufans permitted dropping the lām while keeping the jussive, and Sībawayh permitted that in poetry; and all of them recited: [al-Wāfir] 94-
محمد تفد نفسك كلّ نفس ... إذا ما خفت من أمر تبالا
(Muḥammad, may every soul be a ransom for your soul, whenever you fear ruin from some matter.)
Abū al-ʿAbbās claimed that this is not permissible, because the jussive-governing particle is not implied.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: The ism of «إن», and the khabar (predicate) is (إِنَّما يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ ناراً). Ibn ʿĀmir, and ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Ibn ʿAbbās [Translator's note: so in the text; perhaps Ibn ʿAyyāsh, i.e. Abū Bakr Shuʿba, is meant], read (وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ) as passive [«وسيُصلَون»]; and Abū Ḥaywa read «وسيُصلّون», for multiplicity.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
(يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ فِي أَوْلادِكُمْ): a statement (khabar) in which there is the sense of obligation; then He made clear what He enjoined on them, and said: (لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ). «مثل» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or by the adverbial phrase (al-ṣifa); outside the Qur'an the accusative is permissible, with an implied verb. (فَإِنْ كُنَّ نِساءً): the khabar of «كان», i.e. if the children are women. (فَوْقَ اثْنَتَيْنِ): Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned several views on it. Among them: that «فوق» is redundant (zāʾida); this is wrong, because adverbs are not among the things that are added without meaning. Among them: argument [by analogy] from the sisters; there is no argument in it, because that is a matter of consensus, and so it is conceded for that reason. Among them: that it is a matter of consensus; this is rejected, because what is sound from Ibn ʿAbbās is that he gave the sons half [Translator's note: so in the text («البنين»); the context requires «البنتين», the two daughters], because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: فَإِنْ كُنَّ نِساءً فَوْقَ اثْنَتَيْنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثا ما تَرَكَ; he said: so I do not give the two daughters two-thirds. Among them: that Abū al-ʿAbbās said: in the verse there is what indicates that the two daughters have two-thirds; he said:
since the single [daughter] together with a single son has one-third, we knew that the two daughters have two-thirds. This argument is an error according to the people of reasoning, because the disagreement is about the two daughters and not about the single one; so his opponent would say: if he leaves two daughters and a son, the two daughters have half, so this is evidence that this is their share. The strongest argument that the two daughters have two-thirds is the ḥadīth that is related. The dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz and the Banū Asad is «الثُّلُث» and «الرُّبُع» up to the tenth, and the dialect of the Banū Tamīm and Rabīʿa is «الثُّلْث» with a sukūn on the lām, up to the tenth. One says «ثلثت القوم أثلثهم» (I made the people three / I took a third of them), and «ثلثت الدراهم أثلثها» when you completed them to three, and «أثلثت هي» (they became three); except that for a hundred and a thousand they said «مأيتها» and «أمأت», «آلفتها» and «ألفت». (وَإِنْ كانَتْ واحِدَةً فَلَهَا النِّصْفُ): this is a good reading, i.e. and if the [female] child is one, like (فَإِنْ كُنَّ نِساءً). The people of Medina read وَإِنْ كانَتْ واحِدَةً [«واحدةٌ», in the nominative], with «كانت» in the sense of «وقعت» (occurred), like «كان الأمر» (the matter happened). Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read فَلَهَا النِّصْفُ [Translator's note: presumably «النُّصف», with ḍamma on the nūn]. The people of Kufa read فَلِأُمِّهِ الثُّلُثُ [«فلإمّه», with kasra on the hamza], and this is a dialect which Sībawayh related. Al-Kisāʾī said: it is the dialect of many of Hawāzin and Hudhayl. Abū Jaʿfar said: since the lām has a kasra and is joined to the word, they disliked a ḍamma after a kasra, so they replaced the ḍamma with a kasra, because there is no fiʿul pattern in the language; and whoever reads with ḍamma brings it according to the original, and because the lām is separable, since it enters upon the noun. Mujāhid, ʿĀṣim and Ibn Kathīr read مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِي بِها أَوْ دَيْنٍ as passive [«يُوصَى»], and al-Ḥasan read يُوصِي بِها for multiplicity [«يُوَصِّي»]. (فَرِيضَةً): a maṣdar (verbal noun). (إِنَّ اللَّهَ): the ism of «إنّ». (كانَ عَلِيماً): the khabar of «كان», and the ism of «كان» is latent in it, and the clause is the khabar of «إنّ». Outside the Qur'an «إنّ الله كان عليمٌ حكيمٌ» is permissible, treating «كان» as cancelled (ilghāʾ). The exegetes say: the meaning of «كان عليما حكيما» is «He has never ceased [to be]». The doctrine of Sībawayh is that they saw wisdom and knowledge, so it was said to them: Allah was like that. Abū al-ʿAbbās said: there is nothing in His saying «كان» that indicates negation of the present and the future. And it has been said: «كان» is used to inform about the present, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَنْ كانَ فِي الْمَهْدِ صَبِيًّا [Maryam: 29].

nahhas-irab:146-146.t:
إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تابُوا: an exception. فأولئك مع المؤمنين: i.e. "those believe along with the believers".
وَسَوْفَ يُؤْتِ اللَّهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَجْراً عَظِيماً: two objects (mafʿūlān). The yāʾ of «يؤتي» was omitted in the codex because it is omitted in pronunciation owing to the meeting of two quiescent letters. The people of Medina drop it when pausing and keep the like of it in continuous recitation; al-Kisāʾī gave as their reason that the pause is a place of omission — do you not see that you drop the case-ending in the pause?

nahhas-irab:147-147.t: ما يَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ بِعَذابِكُمْ: ما is in the position of the accusative. The meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, does not benefit from punishing you, nor from your wrongdoing, so why would He punish you إِنْ شَكَرْتُمْ وَآمَنْتُمْ? وَكانَ اللَّهُ شاكِراً عَلِيماً: i.e. He thanks His servants for obeying Him, and the meaning of "He thanks them" is "He rewards them".

nahhas-irab:148-148.t: لا يُحِبُّ اللَّهُ الْجَهْرَ بِالسُّوءِ: i.e. He does not want anyone to speak publicly of evil in speech. The statement is complete; then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said إِلَّا مَنْ ظُلِمَ: an exception not from the first [category], in the position of the accusative, i.e. "but whoever has been wronged may say: so-and-so wronged me in such-and-such". «من» may also be in the position of the nominative, the implied form being "Allah does not like that anyone speak publicly of evil except one who has been wronged". Making the lām quiescent is allowed [i.e. «ظُلْمَ»]. Whoever reads إِلَّا مَنْ ظُلِمَ [Translator's note: printed identically in the source; the reading meant is the active «ظَلَمَ»] may not make the lām quiescent, because of the lightness of the fatḥa; and its implied form is "what would Allah do with punishing you, except whoever has done wrong".

nahhas-irab:149-149.t: إِنْ تُبْدُوا خَيْراً: i.e. [instead] of evil speech. أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ أَوْ تَعْفُوا عَنْ سُوءٍ: i.e. if you show good, that is better than evil speech; or you conceal it, or you pardon an evil that has befallen you — then Allah pardons you for your pardoning.

nahhas-irab:150-150.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ: the noun (ism) of «إنّ», and the clause is the khabar (predicate). وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يُفَرِّقُوا بَيْنَ اللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ: i.e. between belief in Allah and [belief in] His messengers. وَيَقُولُونَ نُؤْمِنُ بِبَعْضٍ وَنَكْفُرُ بِبَعْضٍ: these are the Jews; they believed in Moses, peace be upon him, and disbelieved in Jesus and Muḥammad ﷺ. وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا بَيْنَ ذلِكَ: He did not say ذينك ("those two"), because ذلك can be used for two, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said بَيْنَ ذلِكَ [al-Baqara: 68] in «Sūrat al-Baqara»; had it been ذينك, it would have been allowed. The meaning is: "and they want to take a way between belief and denial".

nahhas-irab:151-151.t: أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْكافِرُونَ حَقًّا: because their belief in Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, does not benefit them if they disbelieve in His Messenger; and if they disbelieve in His Messenger, they have disbelieved in Him, Mighty and Majestic is He, because He is the One who sent the Messenger and sent down the Book upon him; and they disbelieved in every messenger who gave glad tidings of that Messenger. For this reason they became the disbelievers in truth. The implied form is "I have said a true saying" (قلت قولا حقا), and what precedes it indicates it. وَأَعْتَدْنا لِلْكافِرِينَ عَذاباً مُهِيناً: لِلْكافِرِينَ stands in the place of the second object.

nahhas-irab:152-152.t: وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: a mubtadaʾ (subject) in the position of the nominative; or, if you wish, it is in the position of the accusative by an implied verb explained by what follows it.

nahhas-irab:153-153.t:
يَسْئَلُكَ أَهْلُ الْكِتابِ أَنْ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ كِتاباً: these are the Jews; they asked the Prophet ﷺ to ascend to heaven while they watched him [go up] without a book, and to come down with a book, in order to obstruct him ﷺ. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that their forefathers had obstructed Moses, peace be upon him, with greater than this. فَقالُوا أَرِنَا اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً: جهرة is an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "an open seeing". As for the view of Abū ʿUbayda that the implied form is "they said openly" — [then it is] in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) [Translator's note: the sentence appears incomplete in the source].
وَأَرِنا with the rāʾ quiescent is far-fetched in Arabic, because it is an omission after an omission. فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ بِظُلْمِهِمْ: i.e. because of the enormity of what they came with. ثُمَّ اتَّخَذُوا الْعِجْلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما جاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّناتُ: i.e. the proofs that there is none worthy of worship except Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. فَعَفَوْنا عَنْ ذلِكَ وَآتَيْنا مُوسى سُلْطاناً مُبِيناً: of the signs that he brought. A sign is called sulṭān (authority) because the one who brings it prevails by the proof, and it overpowers hearts, in that one knows that it is not within human power to bring the like of it.

nahhas-irab:154-154.t: وَقُلْنا لَهُمُ ادْخُلُوا الْبابَ سُجَّداً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَقُلْنا لَهُمْ لا تَعْدُوا فِي السَّبْتِ: from عدا تعدو; and تعدّوا [is also read], whose original is تعتدوا, the tāʾ having been assimilated into the dāl. Making the ʿayn quiescent is not allowed, and there is no way of combining two quiescent letters in this; whoever reads it so only attempts an error.

nahhas-irab:155-155.t: فَبِما نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثاقَهُمْ: genitive by the bāʾ, and «ما» is redundant (zāʾida). وَكُفْرِهِمْ: conjoined (maʿṭūf); and likewise وَقَتْلِهِمُ.

nahhas-irab:157-158.t:
«إنّ» [Translator's note: i.e. in إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا الْمَسِيحَ] takes a kasra because it begins [a clause] after "saying", and its fatḥa is a dialectal form. رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: a badal (substitute); or, if you wish, in the sense of "I mean" (أعني). وَما قَتَلُوهُ وَما صَلَبُوهُ وَلكِنْ شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ: various narrations have been related about the resemblance that occurred. Among them: when their leaders lost [track of] the Messiah, they took a man, killed him, dressed him in clothes like the clothes of the Messiah, crucified him on a raised piece of wood, and prevented the people from coming near him lest they be found out; then they buried him at night. And it was said: the Messiah, peace be upon him, was imprisoned with Caesar's deputy, and the Jews gathered before him; he imagined that they wanted his release, so he said to them: "I will let him go for you." They said: "No, we want him killed." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, raised him to Himself, i.e. came between them and him. Caesar's deputy then took a man, killed him and said to them: "I have killed him" — out of fear of them [Translator's note: the source reads «خوفا منه», "out of fear of him"]. So he is the one who made it seem to them. It may be that he believed in him and released him, so he was raised, and they were deceived by someone else who had deserved death in his prison; and it may be that he refrained from killing him because of the signs he saw. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ لَفِي شَكٍّ مِنْهُ ما لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ — the statement is complete. Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said إِلَّا اتِّباعَ الظَّنِّ: an exception not from the first [category], in the position of the accusative; and it may be in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute), i.e. "they have no knowledge of it except following conjecture". Sībawayh recited: [al-Rajaz] 110-
وبلدة ليس بها أنيس ... إلّا اليعافير وإلّا العيس
(And many a land in which there is no companion, except gazelles and white camels.)
وَما قَتَلُوهُ يَقِيناً: an adjective (naʿt) of a maṣdar (verbal noun), and there are two implied forms for it. The clearer of them is that the implied form is "Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said this as a certain saying". The other view is that the meaning is "and they did not know it with certain knowledge". Al-Aʿshā related from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, from ʿĀṣim: بَلْ رَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزاً حَكِيماً without assimilation [of the lām of بل into the rāʾ]. Assimilation is better, because of the closeness of the lām to the rāʾ, and because the rāʾ has trilling (takrīr), so assimilation into it is good. وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزاً: i.e. able to protect His friends from their enemies, and nothing prevents Him from that and no one overcomes Him. حَكِيماً: in how He manages the affairs of His creation.
